reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope and evidence inherited from the supplied records
reasoning_steps.argument: Use U and R1 through R13 solely as identifiers for the fourteen original personnel. U is the person reported to require urgent surgery; the other identifiers imply no diagnoses or fitness. The brief supplies no supported clinical deadlines, safe-space map, qualified residual roster, provider capacity, or operating windows. Artifact 19b9d97c-c0c2-4db9-89b1-a25682689249 identifies the common-schedule requirement but supplies no actual schedule. Artifact bafe20fc-ca46-4eaf-8d1f-f2a5d717c3df supplies S-plus and conditional policy priorities, not accepted arrangements or national preferences. The original historical material remains unavailable, including explicitly truncated material in 1613e7fa-b015-41cf-8c06-c549b8921eff. Missing content and omitted obligations remain unassessed.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Define the three candidates and the state they must preserve
reasoning_steps.argument: N selects a departing set Q containing U and every original-crew escort who leaves, with 1 ≤ |Q| < 14, delivers specified effective support, and sustains the remaining personnel through an explicit review horizon h. E removes all fourteen and completes safe reception and indicated care. E after N removes everyone still aboard while also completing the outstanding care obligations for those already departed. At time t, record state x(t): personnel locations and capabilities, patient support needs, safe spaces and routes, available providers and equipment, consumable stocks, ongoing tasks, weather constraints, and assessment validity. Thus E after N is E from x(t), not a fresh copy of E from x(0). If all fourteen must depart for effective care or functional safety, that variant is E rather than N.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Specify the conditional model inputs without assuming feasibility
reasoning_steps.argument: For each specified provider and mode, define a finite collection of mandatory and contingent tasks, their precedence relations, duration bounds, release conditions, capacity demands, stock consumption, and effects on x(t). Define an uncertainty set Ω describing the conditions for which a certificate is claimed. For the conditional result, qualified assessments must conservatively cover those conditions, including deterioration during waiting and execution. No existence of a feasible schedule is assumed. Provider-specific parameters remain symbolic; no transport mode, replacement crew, operating limit, or assessment outcome is supplied by this model. If the model omits a necessary task or hazard, its certificate does not cover that omission.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Task precedence and patient-care endpoints
reasoning_steps.argument: For task j, let s_j and f_j be its start and finish, with duration determined within the assessed envelope. A precedence edge i → j requires s_j ≥ f_i. A typical transfer chain includes required preparation and support, movement along an assessed route, embarkation, transit, clinical handover, and the clinician-defined intervention endpoint. Receiving-service preparation can occur in parallel, but care cannot be credited before the necessary patient arrival and clinical prerequisites. For every person, define mandatory endpoints for leaving unsafe spaces, supported transfer, reception, and indicated treatment or continuing support. For U, the operative endpoint must be clinician-defined: facility arrival is not surgery. Under N, remaining personnel additionally need effective support and safe occupancy through h. Treatment deadlines may concern initiation or completion; the model must use the endpoint actually specified by clinicians.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Shared resources and inventories
reasoning_steps.argument: For each renewable resource r, require that the total demand of simultaneously active tasks not exceed its available capacity K_r(t, x, ω). Candidate resources include transport capacity, transfer equipment, a usable transfer location, medical attendants, clinical-service capacity, communications capability, and essential crew functions; their actual availability is unknown. A provider transporting U remains committed until its assessed release or return, even after U reaches care. Represent that commitment by an occupation interval or explicit travel and recovery tasks, but do not count it twice. Consumables require stock accounting, not renewable-capacity accounting: delivered usable stock plus initial stock must cover consumption at every time. Support delivered too late, unusable in the occupied space, or consumed by another task cannot also sustain the residual crew.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Residual-crew coverage is a time-dependent assignment constraint
reasoning_steps.argument: Let y_if(t) indicate assignment of person i to essential function f, and let v_if(t, x, ω) indicate qualified, physically accessible, clinically compatible availability. Require y_if ≤ v_if and sufficient coverage for every required function throughout its assessed interval. Impose incompatibility constraints so the same person is not simultaneously credited with mutually exclusive tasks. Required intervals and coverage levels must come from responsible specialists and command, not an invented headcount. A departing escort becomes unavailable aboard; a patient cannot be counted as fit without assessment. Fatigue, movement time, loss of access to a station, and reassignment delays also constrain coverage. N passes only if these assignments work through h and through every transition for which fallback preservation is claimed.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Space, route, and operation-specific weather constraints
reasoning_steps.argument: Each task needs an assessed usable location and, where movement is required, a connected usable route. Every person must occupy an assessed permissible space while aboard, including during waiting. For each operation j, define its permitted weather windows W_j(ω), potentially a union of disjoint intervals. Its actual execution interval must lie within an applicable window, with any stricter continuity requirement explicitly represented. Approach, patient transfer, departure, transit, and reception can have different limits. A route or transfer point may be lost before the wreck sinks; a transfer window may close before the forecast storm arrives. Accordingly, neither six hours nor eighteen hours supplies a model deadline or operating window. Waiting itself must remain physically supportable.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Last-person extraction and shutdown of essential functions
reasoning_steps.argument: For E, let ℓ_i be completion of person i's safe transfer off the wreck and let ℓ_last = max_i ℓ_i. All transfers, including the last, must fit their route, location, weather, and support constraints. The last group must have sufficient capacity and a valid transfer method; no task may silently require an original crew member to remain aboard after that person's own final departure. Essential function coverage persists until a specialist-assessed termination or handover condition, not automatically until everyone else leaves. Any final task must be performable without destroying its performer's extraction route. After ℓ_last, transit, reception, and care obligations can remain outstanding; they continue consuming resources. For E after N, already departed personnel remain in the overall accounting until their mandatory endpoints are completed.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Switching is an explicit transition, not a reset
reasoning_steps.argument: At a switch time τ, preserve every completed action and ongoing commitment in x(τ). Add the necessary switch tasks: communicating the changed plan, safe suspension or completion of ongoing work, recovering or reconfiguring resources, relocating personnel, and preparing the remaining transfers. These can overlap only when their resources and precedence permit. If a single aggregate switch delay δ is used, it must bound those tasks on their actual critical path rather than sum parallel work or omit resource recovery. A switch can occur after a partial N attempt, not only after N completes. The combined schedule must include U's continuing transport and care alongside evacuation of the residual crew. Any claimed protection through the switch also needs separate access and authorization checks.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Information-compatible policies rather than hindsight schedules
reasoning_steps.argument: A policy π maps observed history to authorized candidate actions; physical testing does not itself grant that authorization. For any two modeled states whose observed histories are identical through time t, π must choose identical actions through that time. Observation events must be specified, such as receipt of a particular assessment at θ, an observed provider return, or observed obstruction. If an expected report is delayed or inconclusive, include that history rather than allowing the policy to branch on unavailable information. The physical preservation test is existence of one such policy satisfying the constraints in every ω within its claimed envelope. Separate feasible schedules chosen after learning ω do not establish that policy. Actual task completions may reveal information and permit subsequent adaptation, but an unobserved future deterioration cannot justify an earlier branch-specific dispatch.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Integrated test and its limited soundness
reasoning_steps.argument: Test N alone through its declared horizon, E from the initial state, and a combined N-prefix-to-E policy separately. For the combined claim, require compatible continuation at every history and switch covered by the asserted fallback envelope, not merely at the most convenient switch time. Obtain endpoint completion bounds from that common policy and apply the saved timing certificate in 13e0b524-a2b6-42db-8742-27709383fe8b, cycle 1, steps 4–5. Use the distinct exclusion test in 0825c224-cda6-4e4a-bc77-c148884e9593, cycle 2, step 10, only with its required bound directions. Under valid inputs, a satisfying policy supports the stated physical certificate because each mandatory physical condition is met by compatible actions. Missing inputs or failure to find such a policy leaves certification open. Infeasibility of a conservative model need not establish real physical impossibility; actual exclusion requires a valid unavoidable contradiction for the specified candidate. No completeness over all possible rescue methods is claimed.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Conditional single-provider conflict
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider only this hypothetical candidate family. One provider B is initially available at the wreck. A dedicated U movement started at s ≥ 0 reaches U's required treatment endpoint at s+a and makes B unavailable for further wreck extraction until s+ρ. No substitute or combined loading mode exists within this example. At time θ, an assessment first reveals either continued safe occupancy through the review horizon or deterioration requiring the residual crew's last transfer by H. The residual evacuation requires uninterrupted use of B for duration e; independent switch preparation takes δ after θ and can overlap B's absence. Assume exact symbolic relations a ≤ D_U < θ < ρ and θ+δ+e ≤ H < ρ+e. All other constraints are assumed satisfied for this local example. These are hypothetical relations, not scenario observations.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Derive the conflict and identify the information trap
reasoning_steps.argument: Starting U's dedicated movement at zero meets its deadline because a ≤ D_U. Any timely start must satisfy s ≤ D_U−a < θ, so the dispatch decision precedes the assessment. In the deterioration branch, the residual group's earliest last transfer after dispatch is max(θ+δ, s+ρ)+e. Since s ≥ 0, this is at least ρ+e > H. Thus timely U rescue using this dedicated movement destroys the claimed subsequent evacuation route in that branch. By contrast, θ+δ+e ≤ H shows that the residual evacuation would fit if B were available at θ: the particular obstruction is its continuing commitment to U's movement. A policy cannot dispatch B before θ in the favorable branch but retain it before θ in the adverse branch when those histories are indistinguishable. This refutes that candidate's assured N-to-E fallback, not the value of rescuing U and not every possible assistance policy.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Bounds that would resolve physical compatibility
reasoning_steps.argument: For a real version of this candidate, certification needs a completion upper bound a+ for U against its deadline lower bound L_U, an absolute upper bound r+ on B's renewed availability, a switch-preparation upper bound δ+, and a compatible residual-extraction upper bound e+. A sufficient last-transfer check is max(θ+δ+, r+)+e+ plus the selected reserve no later than a defensible safe-window/deadline lower bound H−, together with all intermediate windows, coverage, and downstream care checks. Conversely, with unavoidable earliest readiness r−, switch lower bound δ−, extraction lower bound e−, and latest possible transfer deadline H+, max(θ+δ−, r−)+e− > H+ excludes this continuation under those conditions. Here θ must be the actual or properly bounded observation time. A substitute provider's supported readiness and capacity, a valid combined-loading mode, earlier reliable warning, or a different clinically acceptable U route can remove the contradiction, but each changes the candidate and needs its own check. Unknown bounds leave the choice uncertified.

reasoning_steps.title: 15. Direct E and the distribution-of-risk judgment
reasoning_steps.argument: Let direct E have last-transfer completion e0 and U's required-care completion a_E, measured from now. If supported bounds place e0 within every extraction constraint and a_E within U's clinical deadline, and all other endpoints and gates pass, direct E offers a way around this particular resource conflict, though it does not preserve the occupied position. If direct E saves the extraction opportunity but a defensible earliest a_E exceeds U's latest clinical deadline, direct E also fails a mandatory endpoint; it must not be called successful full rescue. Choosing it over dedicated U rescue would then allocate harm differently. The responsible Philippine authorities must explicitly judge exposure of U versus the remaining personnel, the admissibility of an N attempt without an assured fallback, and whether possible physical exclusion is accepted for rescue. Washington and any other provider separately authorize their contributions and exposure. The judgment must identify affected people, unmet endpoints, uncertainty, chosen limits, and delegated emergency decisions if communication fails. A generic survival-first slogan does not resolve that distribution, and no unsupported casualty probabilities or weighted score are supplied here.

reasoning_steps.title: 16. Access, authority, and durable outcomes remain separate
reasoning_steps.argument: Report results as separate fields: physical certificate, implemented access for each movement, legal assessment, Philippine authorization, each provider's national authorization, accepted risk judgment, and durable-mission assessment. S-plus requests N and E protection through last-person extraction and outbound transit; the older N-only specification is stale as a description of the revised request, but its actual-access objection remains unresolved. Bargaining willingness requires acceptance and local implementation; refusal of S-plus does not exclude every narrower arrangement; assent contradicted by obstruction cannot support reliance on that movement. A physical certificate establishes none of these behavioral or legal gates. Continued occupancy additionally needs sustainable repair and repeatable access; evacuation-and-return additionally needs actual protected return and implementation. Evacuation without an implemented successor can preserve lives while sacrificing presence. Reserved claims do not fill that physical gap. Firing order remains unresolved for accountability and legal application, without preventing urgent care requests.

reasoning_steps.argument: The next discriminating analytical test is to evaluate a specified N prefix, direct E, and E after that prefix against the same symbolic task and observation record, expressly identifying the first irreversible resource commitment and the latest supported switch. An affirmative physical result supports consideration, not automatic selection. A proved candidate-specific conflict requires a changed method or an explicit loss-limitation judgment, not continued description of E as assured. The supplied batch's overlapping duties concerning clinical and structural bounds, providers, residual coverage, switching, and last-person extraction are sharpened but remain empirically unresolved. Access, authority, legal sources, attribution, political standards, recurrence, enforceability, domestic acceptance, and historical completeness likewise remain open. In particular, ledger entries e0f2b55cd9d6c187926c0771d2dd71a65c1de224ae0c8ae61aa204b496ef2944 and fd246f7c04254c301e5b947ca8b970b3d0c82b7c189b86207a5d688b9baf92da receive an explicit test, not a positive availability finding. Confidence is high in the conditional resource conflict and information-compatibility distinction, but actual N/E feasibility is indeterminate. Neither durable full success nor the actual seizure-or-war branch is established.

skeptic_output.response:
Cycle 5 substantially completes the requested symbolic scheduling exercise. The model distinguishes N, direct E, and evacuation after an N attempt; preserves outstanding care obligations; accounts for shared resources, residual-crew functions, operation-specific windows, switching, and last-person extraction; and requires decisions to respect the information actually available. These are useful advances over separate endpoint checks.

The local resource-conflict deduction is sound within its stated candidate family. Timely dedicated rescue of U requires dispatch before θ. In the deterioration branch, the provider cannot support the subsequent residual evacuation before its renewed availability, giving last-transfer completion at least ρ+e>H. The result defeats an assured post-assessment evacuation continuation for that candidate. It does not exclude anticipatory complete evacuation, another provider, combined loading, another clinical route, or rescue generally. The Investigator appropriately treats those as different candidates requiring separate checks, not as capabilities already available.

The bounds in step 14 correctly distinguish sufficient certification from exclusion. Upper completion and readiness bounds against deadline lower bounds can support certification; unavoidable completion lower bounds beyond deadline upper bounds can exclude the specified continuation. Failure of a conservative model or absence of a demonstrated policy does not establish physical impossibility. The information-compatibility requirement also repairs the earlier concern that separately feasible hindsight schedules need not define an executable policy.

The saved derivations remain usable without rewriting: artifact 13e0b524-a2b6-42db-8742-27709383fe8b, cycle 1, steps 4–5, supplies the conditional timing certificate; artifact 0825c224-cda6-4e4a-bc77-c148884e9593, cycle 2, steps 10–11, supplies the distinct timing-exclusion and changed-state tests. Artifact 19b9d97c-c0c2-4db9-89b1-a25682689249, cycle 4, establishes why independent favorable checks are insufficient. Their visible arguments support these limited deductions, not actual rescue availability.

The full research objective remains partial. No supported inputs establish an executable N or E policy, and physical feasibility would not establish implemented access, lawful authority, acceptable distribution of risk, alliance credibility, or durable preservation without rewarding coercion. The current symbolic subtask need not be repeated. The next advance should return to the broader mission: compare the previously proposed continuing-occupancy repair regime, evacuation-and-return regime, and explicit loss limitation against the same response models and political standards. This can expose which commitments and concessions are indispensable without inventing observations.

reasoning_assessments.rationale: The brief and visible extracts supply neither the required individual assessments nor an actual common schedule. The cited cycle 3 proposal is explicitly unimplemented, and the historical extract expressly omits material. The step preserves these limitations.

The candidate definitions consistently distinguish continued occupancy from complete departure. Counting escorts in Q and retaining departed patients' outstanding care obligations prevents N-to-E switching from resetting personnel or resource accounting.

Accepted only as the explicitly listed conservative-assessment and complete-model premises of the conditional claim. The step does not assume a feasible schedule or establish any scenario-specific parameter.

Precedence constraints prevent a dependent operation from preceding its prerequisites while allowing independent preparation in parallel. Clinician-defined treatment and continuing-support endpoints correctly prevent departure or facility arrival from substituting for effective care.

Simultaneous demand must fit available renewable capacity, whereas consumables require cumulative stock accounting. Explicit occupation intervals or recovery tasks correctly retain a provider's commitment after initial patient delivery without double counting it.

Availability, qualification, access, clinical compatibility, and incompatible simultaneous assignments are necessary constraints on functional coverage. A departing escort cannot remain credited aboard, and a numerical headcount cannot replace these time-dependent assignments.

Operations require usable locations, routes, and activity-specific windows throughout execution. Their loss can precede sinking or storm arrival, so neither announced scenario time establishes the needed window. Including safe waiting closes an otherwise omitted physical dependency.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope and evidence inherited from the supplied records
reasoning_steps.argument: Use U and R1 through R13 solely as identifiers for the fourteen original personnel. U is the person reported to require urgent surgery; the other identifiers imply no diagnoses or fitness. The brief supplies no supported clinical deadlines, safe-space map, qualified residual roster, provider capacity, or operating windows. Artifact 19b9d97c-c0c2-4db9-89b1-a25682689249 identifies the common-schedule requirement but supplies no actual schedule. Artifact bafe20fc-ca46-4eaf-8d1f-f2a5d717c3df supplies S-plus and conditional policy priorities, not accepted arrangements or national preferences. The original historical material remains unavailable, including explicitly truncated material in 1613e7fa-b015-41cf-8c06-c549b8921eff. Missing content and omitted obligations remain unassessed.

review.rationale: The brief and visible extracts supply neither the required individual assessments nor an actual common schedule. The cited cycle 3 proposal is explicitly unimplemented, and the historical extract expressly omits material. The step preserves these limitations.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Define the three candidates and the state they must preserve
reasoning_steps.argument: N selects a departing set Q containing U and every original-crew escort who leaves, with 1 ≤ |Q| < 14, delivers specified effective support, and sustains the remaining personnel through an explicit review horizon h. E removes all fourteen and completes safe reception and indicated care. E after N removes everyone still aboard while also completing the outstanding care obligations for those already departed. At time t, record state x(t): personnel locations and capabilities, patient support needs, safe spaces and routes, available providers and equipment, consumable stocks, ongoing tasks, weather constraints, and assessment validity. Thus E after N is E from x(t), not a fresh copy of E from x(0). If all fourteen must depart for effective care or functional safety, that variant is E rather than N.

review.rationale: The candidate definitions consistently distinguish continued occupancy from complete departure. Counting escorts in Q and retaining departed patients' outstanding care obligations prevents N-to-E switching from resetting personnel or resource accounting.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Specify the conditional model inputs without assuming feasibility
reasoning_steps.argument: For each specified provider and mode, define a finite collection of mandatory and contingent tasks, their precedence relations, duration bounds, release conditions, capacity demands, stock consumption, and effects on x(t). Define an uncertainty set Ω describing the conditions for which a certificate is claimed. For the conditional result, qualified assessments must conservatively cover those conditions, including deterioration during waiting and execution. No existence of a feasible schedule is assumed. Provider-specific parameters remain symbolic; no transport mode, replacement crew, operating limit, or assessment outcome is supplied by this model. If the model omits a necessary task or hazard, its certificate does not cover that omission.

review.rationale: Accepted only as the explicitly listed conservative-assessment and complete-model premises of the conditional claim. The step does not assume a feasible schedule or establish any scenario-specific parameter.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Task precedence and patient-care endpoints
reasoning_steps.argument: For task j, let s_j and f_j be its start and finish, with duration determined within the assessed envelope. A precedence edge i → j requires s_j ≥ f_i. A typical transfer chain includes required preparation and support, movement along an assessed route, embarkation, transit, clinical handover, and the clinician-defined intervention endpoint. Receiving-service preparation can occur in parallel, but care cannot be credited before the necessary patient arrival and clinical prerequisites. For every person, define mandatory endpoints for leaving unsafe spaces, supported transfer, reception, and indicated treatment or continuing support. For U, the operative endpoint must be clinician-defined: facility arrival is not surgery. Under N, remaining personnel additionally need effective support and safe occupancy through h. Treatment deadlines may concern initiation or completion; the model must use the endpoint actually specified by clinicians.

review.rationale: Precedence constraints prevent a dependent operation from preceding its prerequisites while allowing independent preparation in parallel. Clinician-defined treatment and continuing-support endpoints correctly prevent departure or facility arrival from substituting for effective care.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Shared resources and inventories
reasoning_steps.argument: For each renewable resource r, require that the total demand of simultaneously active tasks not exceed its available capacity K_r(t, x, ω). Candidate resources include transport capacity, transfer equipment, a usable transfer location, medical attendants, clinical-service capacity, communications capability, and essential crew functions; their actual availability is unknown. A provider transporting U remains committed until its assessed release or return, even after U reaches care. Represent that commitment by an occupation interval or explicit travel and recovery tasks, but do not count it twice. Consumables require stock accounting, not renewable-capacity accounting: delivered usable stock plus initial stock must cover consumption at every time. Support delivered too late, unusable in the occupied space, or consumed by another task cannot also sustain the residual crew.

review.rationale: Simultaneous demand must fit available renewable capacity, whereas consumables require cumulative stock accounting. Explicit occupation intervals or recovery tasks correctly retain a provider's commitment after initial patient delivery without double counting it.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Residual-crew coverage is a time-dependent assignment constraint
reasoning_steps.argument: Let y_if(t) indicate assignment of person i to essential function f, and let v_if(t, x, ω) indicate qualified, physically accessible, clinically compatible availability. Require y_if ≤ v_if and sufficient coverage for every required function throughout its assessed interval. Impose incompatibility constraints so the same person is not simultaneously credited with mutually exclusive tasks. Required intervals and coverage levels must come from responsible specialists and command, not an invented headcount. A departing escort becomes unavailable aboard; a patient cannot be counted as fit without assessment. Fatigue, movement time, loss of access to a station, and reassignment delays also constrain coverage. N passes only if these assignments work through h and through every transition for which fallback preservation is claimed.

review.rationale: Availability, qualification, access, clinical compatibility, and incompatible simultaneous assignments are necessary constraints on functional coverage. A departing escort cannot remain credited aboard, and a numerical headcount cannot replace these time-dependent assignments.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Space, route, and operation-specific weather constraints
reasoning_steps.argument: Each task needs an assessed usable location and, where movement is required, a connected usable route. Every person must occupy an assessed permissible space while aboard, including during waiting. For each operation j, define its permitted weather windows W_j(ω), potentially a union of disjoint intervals. Its actual execution interval must lie within an applicable window, with any stricter continuity requirement explicitly represented. Approach, patient transfer, departure, transit, and reception can have different limits. A route or transfer point may be lost before the wreck sinks; a transfer window may close before the forecast storm arrives. Accordingly, neither six hours nor eighteen hours supplies a model deadline or operating window. Waiting itself must remain physically supportable.

review.rationale: Operations require usable locations, routes, and activity-specific windows throughout execution. Their loss can precede sinking or storm arrival, so neither announced scenario time establishes the needed window. Including safe waiting closes an otherwise omitted physical dependency.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Last-person extraction and shutdown of essential functions
reasoning_steps.argument: For E, let ℓ_i be completion of person i's safe transfer off the wreck and let ℓ_last = max_i ℓ_i. All transfers, including the last, must fit their route, location, weather, and support constraints. The last group must have sufficient capacity and a valid transfer method; no task may silently require an original crew member to remain aboard after that person's own final departure. Essential function coverage persists until a specialist-assessed termination or handover condition, not automatically until everyone else leaves. Any final task must be performable without destroying its performer's extraction route. After ℓ_last, transit, reception, and care obligations can remain outstanding; they continue consuming resources. For E after N, already departed personnel remain in the overall accounting until their mandatory endpoints are completed.

review.rationale: Taking the maximum individual transfer completion accounts for the last departing person, but does not finish downstream transit or care. Requiring a feasible termination or handover of essential functions avoids assigning an impossible final task to someone already departed.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Switching is an explicit transition, not a reset
reasoning_steps.argument: At a switch time τ, preserve every completed action and ongoing commitment in x(τ). Add the necessary switch tasks: communicating the changed plan, safe suspension or completion of ongoing work, recovering or reconfiguring resources, relocating personnel, and preparing the remaining transfers. These can overlap only when their resources and precedence permit. If a single aggregate switch delay δ is used, it must bound those tasks on their actual critical path rather than sum parallel work or omit resource recovery. A switch can occur after a partial N attempt, not only after N completes. The combined schedule must include U's continuing transport and care alongside evacuation of the residual crew. Any claimed protection through the switch also needs separate access and authorization checks.

review.rationale: Completed actions and ongoing commitments persist through switching. Explicit transition tasks and critical-path accounting correctly avoid treating parallel preparation as serial delay or omitting provider recovery and continuing patient care.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Information-compatible policies rather than hindsight schedules
reasoning_steps.argument: A policy π maps observed history to authorized candidate actions; physical testing does not itself grant that authorization. For any two modeled states whose observed histories are identical through time t, π must choose identical actions through that time. Observation events must be specified, such as receipt of a particular assessment at θ, an observed provider return, or observed obstruction. If an expected report is delayed or inconclusive, include that history rather than allowing the policy to branch on unavailable information. The physical preservation test is existence of one such policy satisfying the constraints in every ω within its claimed envelope. Separate feasible schedules chosen after learning ω do not establish that policy. Actual task completions may reveal information and permit subsequent adaptation, but an unobserved future deterioration cannot justify an earlier branch-specific dispatch.

review.rationale: Identical observed histories cannot support different prior decisions by one executable policy. Explicit observation events and delayed-report histories therefore distinguish nonanticipative policies from separately selected hindsight schedules. The universal requirement is properly limited to the declared envelope.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Integrated test and its limited soundness
reasoning_steps.argument: Test N alone through its declared horizon, E from the initial state, and a combined N-prefix-to-E policy separately. For the combined claim, require compatible continuation at every history and switch covered by the asserted fallback envelope, not merely at the most convenient switch time. Obtain endpoint completion bounds from that common policy and apply the saved timing certificate in 13e0b524-a2b6-42db-8742-27709383fe8b, cycle 1, steps 4–5. Use the distinct exclusion test in 0825c224-cda6-4e4a-bc77-c148884e9593, cycle 2, step 10, only with its required bound directions. Under valid inputs, a satisfying policy supports the stated physical certificate because each mandatory physical condition is met by compatible actions. Missing inputs or failure to find such a policy leaves certification open. Infeasibility of a conservative model need not establish real physical impossibility; actual exclusion requires a valid unavoidable contradiction for the specified candidate. No completeness over all possible rescue methods is claimed.

review.rationale: Given the listed model-validity premises, a single policy meeting every mandatory modeled constraint supplies exactly the limited physical certificate claimed. The saved timing tests retain their correct bound directions, and conservative-model infeasibility is correctly distinguished from unavoidable real-world exclusion.
review.objection: No actual satisfying policy or supported input envelope is supplied; the conclusion is conditional soundness, not scenario-specific certification.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Conditional single-provider conflict
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider only this hypothetical candidate family. One provider B is initially available at the wreck. A dedicated U movement started at s ≥ 0 reaches U's required treatment endpoint at s+a and makes B unavailable for further wreck extraction until s+ρ. No substitute or combined loading mode exists within this example. At time θ, an assessment first reveals either continued safe occupancy through the review horizon or deterioration requiring the residual crew's last transfer by H. The residual evacuation requires uninterrupted use of B for duration e; independent switch preparation takes δ after θ and can overlap B's absence. Assume exact symbolic relations a ≤ D_U < θ < ρ and θ+δ+e ≤ H < ρ+e. All other constraints are assumed satisfied for this local example. These are hypothetical relations, not scenario observations.

review.rationale: Accepted solely as the exact local premises listed in the explicitly conditional claim: exclusive provider commitment, first informative assessment at θ, post-assessment preparation, and the stated duration and deadline relations. None is inferred as an observation of the fictional crisis.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Derive the conflict and identify the information trap
reasoning_steps.argument: Starting U's dedicated movement at zero meets its deadline because a ≤ D_U. Any timely start must satisfy s ≤ D_U−a < θ, so the dispatch decision precedes the assessment. In the deterioration branch, the residual group's earliest last transfer after dispatch is max(θ+δ, s+ρ)+e. Since s ≥ 0, this is at least ρ+e > H. Thus timely U rescue using this dedicated movement destroys the claimed subsequent evacuation route in that branch. By contrast, θ+δ+e ≤ H shows that the residual evacuation would fit if B were available at θ: the particular obstruction is its continuing commitment to U's movement. A policy cannot dispatch B before θ in the favorable branch but retain it before θ in the adverse branch when those histories are indistinguishable. This refutes that candidate's assured N-to-E fallback, not the value of rescuing U and not every possible assistance policy.

review.rationale: Timeliness requires s+a≤D_U, hence s<θ for nonnegative duration a. For the stipulated post-assessment continuation, completion is at least s+ρ+e≥ρ+e>H. Without that commitment, θ+δ+e≤H permits the residual extraction. Indistinguishable prior histories prevent a branch-specific earlier dispatch.
review.objection: The exclusion concerns the stipulated post-assessment continuation; it does not exclude earlier complete evacuation or alternative candidate families.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Bounds that would resolve physical compatibility
reasoning_steps.argument: For a real version of this candidate, certification needs a completion upper bound a+ for U against its deadline lower bound L_U, an absolute upper bound r+ on B's renewed availability, a switch-preparation upper bound δ+, and a compatible residual-extraction upper bound e+. A sufficient last-transfer check is max(θ+δ+, r+)+e+ plus the selected reserve no later than a defensible safe-window/deadline lower bound H−, together with all intermediate windows, coverage, and downstream care checks. Conversely, with unavoidable earliest readiness r−, switch lower bound δ−, extraction lower bound e−, and latest possible transfer deadline H+, max(θ+δ−, r−)+e− > H+ excludes this continuation under those conditions. Here θ must be the actual or properly bounded observation time. A substitute provider's supported readiness and capacity, a valid combined-loading mode, earlier reliable warning, or a different clinically acceptable U route can remove the contradiction, but each changes the candidate and needs its own check. Unknown bounds leave the choice uncertified.

review.rationale: For the stipulated overlapping-preparation chain, upper readiness and duration bounds give the stated sufficient completion bound. Unavoidable lower readiness and duration bounds beyond a deadline upper bound give a valid exclusion. Intermediate windows, coverage, and downstream care remain expressly required.

reasoning_steps.title: 15. Direct E and the distribution-of-risk judgment
reasoning_steps.argument: Let direct E have last-transfer completion e0 and U's required-care completion a_E, measured from now. If supported bounds place e0 within every extraction constraint and a_E within U's clinical deadline, and all other endpoints and gates pass, direct E offers a way around this particular resource conflict, though it does not preserve the occupied position. If direct E saves the extraction opportunity but a defensible earliest a_E exceeds U's latest clinical deadline, direct E also fails a mandatory endpoint; it must not be called successful full rescue. Choosing it over dedicated U rescue would then allocate harm differently. The responsible Philippine authorities must explicitly judge exposure of U versus the remaining personnel, the admissibility of an N attempt without an assured fallback, and whether possible physical exclusion is accepted for rescue. Washington and any other provider separately authorize their contributions and exposure. The judgment must identify affected people, unmet endpoints, uncertainty, chosen limits, and delegated emergency decisions if communication fails. A generic survival-first slogan does not resolve that distribution, and no unsupported casualty probabilities or weighted score are supplied here.

review.rationale: Direct E avoids this particular resource sequence only if its own extraction and care endpoints pass. If its earliest U-care completion exceeds U's latest deadline, it cannot count as full rescue. Choosing between unmet endpoints is a distribution-of-risk judgment, not an implication of physical feasibility alone.
review.objection: No adopted risk judgment or supported direct-E bounds are supplied.

reasoning_steps.title: 16. Access, authority, and durable outcomes remain separate
reasoning_steps.argument: Report results as separate fields: physical certificate, implemented access for each movement, legal assessment, Philippine authorization, each provider's national authorization, accepted risk judgment, and durable-mission assessment. S-plus requests N and E protection through last-person extraction and outbound transit; the older N-only specification is stale as a description of the revised request, but its actual-access objection remains unresolved. Bargaining willingness requires acceptance and local implementation; refusal of S-plus does not exclude every narrower arrangement; assent contradicted by obstruction cannot support reliance on that movement. A physical certificate establishes none of these behavioral or legal gates. Continued occupancy additionally needs sustainable repair and repeatable access; evacuation-and-return additionally needs actual protected return and implementation. Evacuation without an implemented successor can preserve lives while sacrificing presence. Reserved claims do not fill that physical gap. Firing order remains unresolved for accountability and legal application, without preventing urgent care requests.

review.rationale: The expanded request does not establish accepted access. Physical feasibility cannot supply behavioral implementation, law, national authorization, or sustainable return. The step correctly preserves the distinction between rescued personnel, reserved claims, and continued physical presence.

reasoning_steps.title: 17. Provisional decision consequence and ledger disposition
reasoning_steps.argument: The next discriminating analytical test is to evaluate a specified N prefix, direct E, and E after that prefix against the same symbolic task and observation record, expressly identifying the first irreversible resource commitment and the latest supported switch. An affirmative physical result supports consideration, not automatic selection. A proved candidate-specific conflict requires a changed method or an explicit loss-limitation judgment, not continued description of E as assured. The supplied batch's overlapping duties concerning clinical and structural bounds, providers, residual coverage, switching, and last-person extraction are sharpened but remain empirically unresolved. Access, authority, legal sources, attribution, political standards, recurrence, enforceability, domestic acceptance, and historical completeness likewise remain open. In particular, ledger entries e0f2b55cd9d6c187926c0771d2dd71a65c1de224ae0c8ae61aa204b496ef2944 and fd246f7c04254c301e5b947ca8b970b3d0c82b7c189b86207a5d688b9baf92da receive an explicit test, not a positive availability finding. Confidence is high in the conditional resource conflict and information-compatibility distinction, but actual N/E feasibility is indeterminate. Neither durable full success nor the actual seizure-or-war branch is established.

review.rationale: The proposed comparison follows from the established state and resource dependencies. Candidate-specific exclusion requires revision or an acknowledged risk choice, while a physical pass supports consideration rather than automatic selection. The conclusion correctly retains actual feasibility and durable success as unresolved.

argument_steps.argument: Use U and R1 through R13 solely as identifiers for the fourteen original personnel. U is the person reported to require urgent surgery; the other identifiers imply no diagnoses or fitness. The brief supplies no supported clinical deadlines, safe-space map, qualified residual roster, provider capacity, or operating windows. Artifact 19b9d97c-c0c2-4db9-89b1-a25682689249 identifies the common-schedule requirement but supplies no actual schedule. Artifact bafe20fc-ca46-4eaf-8d1f-f2a5d717c3df supplies S-plus and conditional policy priorities, not accepted arrangements or national preferences. The original historical material remains unavailable, including explicitly truncated material in 1613e7fa-b015-41cf-8c06-c549b8921eff. Missing content and omitted obligations remain unassessed.

review.rationale: The brief and visible extracts supply neither the required individual assessments nor an actual common schedule. The cited cycle 3 proposal is explicitly unimplemented, and the historical extract expressly omits material. The step preserves these limitations.

argument_steps.title: 2. Define the three candidates and the state they must preserve
argument_steps.argument: N selects a departing set Q containing U and every original-crew escort who leaves, with 1 ≤ |Q| < 14, delivers specified effective support, and sustains the remaining personnel through an explicit review horizon h. E removes all fourteen and completes safe reception and indicated care. E after N removes everyone still aboard while also completing the outstanding care obligations for those already departed. At time t, record state x(t): personnel locations and capabilities, patient support needs, safe spaces and routes, available providers and equipment, consumable stocks, ongoing tasks, weather constraints, and assessment validity. Thus E after N is E from x(t), not a fresh copy of E from x(0). If all fourteen must depart for effective care or functional safety, that variant is E rather than N.

review.rationale: The candidate definitions consistently distinguish continued occupancy from complete departure. Counting escorts in Q and retaining departed patients' outstanding care obligations prevents N-to-E switching from resetting personnel or resource accounting.

argument_steps.title: 3. Specify the conditional model inputs without assuming feasibility
argument_steps.argument: For each specified provider and mode, define a finite collection of mandatory and contingent tasks, their precedence relations, duration bounds, release conditions, capacity demands, stock consumption, and effects on x(t). Define an uncertainty set Ω describing the conditions for which a certificate is claimed. For the conditional result, qualified assessments must conservatively cover those conditions, including deterioration during waiting and execution. No existence of a feasible schedule is assumed. Provider-specific parameters remain symbolic; no transport mode, replacement crew, operating limit, or assessment outcome is supplied by this model. If the model omits a necessary task or hazard, its certificate does not cover that omission.

review.rationale: Accepted only as the explicitly listed conservative-assessment and complete-model premises of the conditional claim. The step does not assume a feasible schedule or establish any scenario-specific parameter.

argument_steps.title: 4. Task precedence and patient-care endpoints
argument_steps.argument: For task j, let s_j and f_j be its start and finish, with duration determined within the assessed envelope. A precedence edge i → j requires s_j ≥ f_i. A typical transfer chain includes required preparation and support, movement along an assessed route, embarkation, transit, clinical handover, and the clinician-defined intervention endpoint. Receiving-service preparation can occur in parallel, but care cannot be credited before the necessary patient arrival and clinical prerequisites. For every person, define mandatory endpoints for leaving unsafe spaces, supported transfer, reception, and indicated treatment or continuing support. For U, the operative endpoint must be clinician-defined: facility arrival is not surgery. Under N, remaining personnel additionally need effective support and safe occupancy through h. Treatment deadlines may concern initiation or completion; the model must use the endpoint actually specified by clinicians.

review.rationale: Precedence constraints prevent a dependent operation from preceding its prerequisites while allowing independent preparation in parallel. Clinician-defined treatment and continuing-support endpoints correctly prevent departure or facility arrival from substituting for effective care.

argument_steps.title: 5. Shared resources and inventories
argument_steps.argument: For each renewable resource r, require that the total demand of simultaneously active tasks not exceed its available capacity K_r(t, x, ω). Candidate resources include transport capacity, transfer equipment, a usable transfer location, medical attendants, clinical-service capacity, communications capability, and essential crew functions; their actual availability is unknown. A provider transporting U remains committed until its assessed release or return, even after U reaches care. Represent that commitment by an occupation interval or explicit travel and recovery tasks, but do not count it twice. Consumables require stock accounting, not renewable-capacity accounting: delivered usable stock plus initial stock must cover consumption at every time. Support delivered too late, unusable in the occupied space, or consumed by another task cannot also sustain the residual crew.

review.rationale: Simultaneous demand must fit available renewable capacity, whereas consumables require cumulative stock accounting. Explicit occupation intervals or recovery tasks correctly retain a provider's commitment after initial patient delivery without double counting it.

argument_steps.title: 6. Residual-crew coverage is a time-dependent assignment constraint
argument_steps.argument: Let y_if(t) indicate assignment of person i to essential function f, and let v_if(t, x, ω) indicate qualified, physically accessible, clinically compatible availability. Require y_if ≤ v_if and sufficient coverage for every required function throughout its assessed interval. Impose incompatibility constraints so the same person is not simultaneously credited with mutually exclusive tasks. Required intervals and coverage levels must come from responsible specialists and command, not an invented headcount. A departing escort becomes unavailable aboard; a patient cannot be counted as fit without assessment. Fatigue, movement time, loss of access to a station, and reassignment delays also constrain coverage. N passes only if these assignments work through h and through every transition for which fallback preservation is claimed.

review.rationale: Availability, qualification, access, clinical compatibility, and incompatible simultaneous assignments are necessary constraints on functional coverage. A departing escort cannot remain credited aboard, and a numerical headcount cannot replace these time-dependent assignments.

argument_steps.title: 7. Space, route, and operation-specific weather constraints
argument_steps.argument: Each task needs an assessed usable location and, where movement is required, a connected usable route. Every person must occupy an assessed permissible space while aboard, including during waiting. For each operation j, define its permitted weather windows W_j(ω), potentially a union of disjoint intervals. Its actual execution interval must lie within an applicable window, with any stricter continuity requirement explicitly represented. Approach, patient transfer, departure, transit, and reception can have different limits. A route or transfer point may be lost before the wreck sinks; a transfer window may close before the forecast storm arrives. Accordingly, neither six hours nor eighteen hours supplies a model deadline or operating window. Waiting itself must remain physically supportable.

review.rationale: Operations require usable locations, routes, and activity-specific windows throughout execution. Their loss can precede sinking or storm arrival, so neither announced scenario time establishes the needed window. Including safe waiting closes an otherwise omitted physical dependency.

argument_steps.title: 8. Last-person extraction and shutdown of essential functions
argument_steps.argument: For E, let ℓ_i be completion of person i's safe transfer off the wreck and let ℓ_last = max_i ℓ_i. All transfers, including the last, must fit their route, location, weather, and support constraints. The last group must have sufficient capacity and a valid transfer method; no task may silently require an original crew member to remain aboard after that person's own final departure. Essential function coverage persists until a specialist-assessed termination or handover condition, not automatically until everyone else leaves. Any final task must be performable without destroying its performer's extraction route. After ℓ_last, transit, reception, and care obligations can remain outstanding; they continue consuming resources. For E after N, already departed personnel remain in the overall accounting until their mandatory endpoints are completed.

review.rationale: Taking the maximum individual transfer completion accounts for the last departing person, but does not finish downstream transit or care. Requiring a feasible termination or handover of essential functions avoids assigning an impossible final task to someone already departed.

argument_steps.title: 9. Switching is an explicit transition, not a reset
argument_steps.argument: At a switch time τ, preserve every completed action and ongoing commitment in x(τ). Add the necessary switch tasks: communicating the changed plan, safe suspension or completion of ongoing work, recovering or reconfiguring resources, relocating personnel, and preparing the remaining transfers. These can overlap only when their resources and precedence permit. If a single aggregate switch delay δ is used, it must bound those tasks on their actual critical path rather than sum parallel work or omit resource recovery. A switch can occur after a partial N attempt, not only after N completes. The combined schedule must include U's continuing transport and care alongside evacuation of the residual crew. Any claimed protection through the switch also needs separate access and authorization checks.

review.rationale: Completed actions and ongoing commitments persist through switching. Explicit transition tasks and critical-path accounting correctly avoid treating parallel preparation as serial delay or omitting provider recovery and continuing patient care.

argument_steps.title: 10. Information-compatible policies rather than hindsight schedules
argument_steps.argument: A policy π maps observed history to authorized candidate actions; physical testing does not itself grant that authorization. For any two modeled states whose observed histories are identical through time t, π must choose identical actions through that time. Observation events must be specified, such as receipt of a particular assessment at θ, an observed provider return, or observed obstruction. If an expected report is delayed or inconclusive, include that history rather than allowing the policy to branch on unavailable information. The physical preservation test is existence of one such policy satisfying the constraints in every ω within its claimed envelope. Separate feasible schedules chosen after learning ω do not establish that policy. Actual task completions may reveal information and permit subsequent adaptation, but an unobserved future deterioration cannot justify an earlier branch-specific dispatch.

review.rationale: Identical observed histories cannot support different prior decisions by one executable policy. Explicit observation events and delayed-report histories therefore distinguish nonanticipative policies from separately selected hindsight schedules. The universal requirement is properly limited to the declared envelope.

argument_steps.title: 11. Integrated test and its limited soundness
argument_steps.argument: Test N alone through its declared horizon, E from the initial state, and a combined N-prefix-to-E policy separately. For the combined claim, require compatible continuation at every history and switch covered by the asserted fallback envelope, not merely at the most convenient switch time. Obtain endpoint completion bounds from that common policy and apply the saved timing certificate in 13e0b524-a2b6-42db-8742-27709383fe8b, cycle 1, steps 4–5. Use the distinct exclusion test in 0825c224-cda6-4e4a-bc77-c148884e9593, cycle 2, step 10, only with its required bound directions. Under valid inputs, a satisfying policy supports the stated physical certificate because each mandatory physical condition is met by compatible actions. Missing inputs or failure to find such a policy leaves certification open. Infeasibility of a conservative model need not establish real physical impossibility; actual exclusion requires a valid unavoidable contradiction for the specified candidate. No completeness over all possible rescue methods is claimed.

review.rationale: Given the listed model-validity premises, a single policy meeting every mandatory modeled constraint supplies exactly the limited physical certificate claimed. The saved timing tests retain their correct bound directions, and conservative-model infeasibility is correctly distinguished from unavoidable real-world exclusion.
review.objection: No actual satisfying policy or supported input envelope is supplied; the conclusion is conditional soundness, not scenario-specific certification.

argument_steps.title: 12. Conditional single-provider conflict
argument_steps.argument: Consider only this hypothetical candidate family. One provider B is initially available at the wreck. A dedicated U movement started at s ≥ 0 reaches U's required treatment endpoint at s+a and makes B unavailable for further wreck extraction until s+ρ. No substitute or combined loading mode exists within this example. At time θ, an assessment first reveals either continued safe occupancy through the review horizon or deterioration requiring the residual crew's last transfer by H. The residual evacuation requires uninterrupted use of B for duration e; independent switch preparation takes δ after θ and can overlap B's absence. Assume exact symbolic relations a ≤ D_U < θ < ρ and θ+δ+e ≤ H < ρ+e. All other constraints are assumed satisfied for this local example. These are hypothetical relations, not scenario observations.

review.rationale: Accepted solely as the exact local premises listed in the explicitly conditional claim: exclusive provider commitment, first informative assessment at θ, post-assessment preparation, and the stated duration and deadline relations. None is inferred as an observation of the fictional crisis.

argument_steps.title: 13. Derive the conflict and identify the information trap
argument_steps.argument: Starting U's dedicated movement at zero meets its deadline because a ≤ D_U. Any timely start must satisfy s ≤ D_U−a < θ, so the dispatch decision precedes the assessment. In the deterioration branch, the residual group's earliest last transfer after dispatch is max(θ+δ, s+ρ)+e. Since s ≥ 0, this is at least ρ+e > H. Thus timely U rescue using this dedicated movement destroys the claimed subsequent evacuation route in that branch. By contrast, θ+δ+e ≤ H shows that the residual evacuation would fit if B were available at θ: the particular obstruction is its continuing commitment to U's movement. A policy cannot dispatch B before θ in the favorable branch but retain it before θ in the adverse branch when those histories are indistinguishable. This refutes that candidate's assured N-to-E fallback, not the value of rescuing U and not every possible assistance policy.

review.rationale: Timeliness requires s+a≤D_U, hence s<θ for nonnegative duration a. For the stipulated post-assessment continuation, completion is at least s+ρ+e≥ρ+e>H. Without that commitment, θ+δ+e≤H permits the residual extraction. Indistinguishable prior histories prevent a branch-specific earlier dispatch.
review.objection: The exclusion concerns the stipulated post-assessment continuation; it does not exclude earlier complete evacuation or alternative candidate families.

argument_steps.title: 14. Bounds that would resolve physical compatibility
argument_steps.argument: For a real version of this candidate, certification needs a completion upper bound a+ for U against its deadline lower bound L_U, an absolute upper bound r+ on B's renewed availability, a switch-preparation upper bound δ+, and a compatible residual-extraction upper bound e+. A sufficient last-transfer check is max(θ+δ+, r+)+e+ plus the selected reserve no later than a defensible safe-window/deadline lower bound H−, together with all intermediate windows, coverage, and downstream care checks. Conversely, with unavoidable earliest readiness r−, switch lower bound δ−, extraction lower bound e−, and latest possible transfer deadline H+, max(θ+δ−, r−)+e− > H+ excludes this continuation under those conditions. Here θ must be the actual or properly bounded observation time. A substitute provider's supported readiness and capacity, a valid combined-loading mode, earlier reliable warning, or a different clinically acceptable U route can remove the contradiction, but each changes the candidate and needs its own check. Unknown bounds leave the choice uncertified.

review.rationale: For the stipulated overlapping-preparation chain, upper readiness and duration bounds give the stated sufficient completion bound. Unavoidable lower readiness and duration bounds beyond a deadline upper bound give a valid exclusion. Intermediate windows, coverage, and downstream care remain expressly required.

argument_steps.title: 15. Direct E and the distribution-of-risk judgment
argument_steps.argument: Let direct E have last-transfer completion e0 and U's required-care completion a_E, measured from now. If supported bounds place e0 within every extraction constraint and a_E within U's clinical deadline, and all other endpoints and gates pass, direct E offers a way around this particular resource conflict, though it does not preserve the occupied position. If direct E saves the extraction opportunity but a defensible earliest a_E exceeds U's latest clinical deadline, direct E also fails a mandatory endpoint; it must not be called successful full rescue. Choosing it over dedicated U rescue would then allocate harm differently. The responsible Philippine authorities must explicitly judge exposure of U versus the remaining personnel, the admissibility of an N attempt without an assured fallback, and whether possible physical exclusion is accepted for rescue. Washington and any other provider separately authorize their contributions and exposure. The judgment must identify affected people, unmet endpoints, uncertainty, chosen limits, and delegated emergency decisions if communication fails. A generic survival-first slogan does not resolve that distribution, and no unsupported casualty probabilities or weighted score are supplied here.

review.rationale: Direct E avoids this particular resource sequence only if its own extraction and care endpoints pass. If its earliest U-care completion exceeds U's latest deadline, it cannot count as full rescue. Choosing between unmet endpoints is a distribution-of-risk judgment, not an implication of physical feasibility alone.
review.objection: No adopted risk judgment or supported direct-E bounds are supplied.

argument_steps.title: 16. Access, authority, and durable outcomes remain separate
argument_steps.argument: Report results as separate fields: physical certificate, implemented access for each movement, legal assessment, Philippine authorization, each provider's national authorization, accepted risk judgment, and durable-mission assessment. S-plus requests N and E protection through last-person extraction and outbound transit; the older N-only specification is stale as a description of the revised request, but its actual-access objection remains unresolved. Bargaining willingness requires acceptance and local implementation; refusal of S-plus does not exclude every narrower arrangement; assent contradicted by obstruction cannot support reliance on that movement. A physical certificate establishes none of these behavioral or legal gates. Continued occupancy additionally needs sustainable repair and repeatable access; evacuation-and-return additionally needs actual protected return and implementation. Evacuation without an implemented successor can preserve lives while sacrificing presence. Reserved claims do not fill that physical gap. Firing order remains unresolved for accountability and legal application, without preventing urgent care requests.

review.rationale: The expanded request does not establish accepted access. Physical feasibility cannot supply behavioral implementation, law, national authorization, or sustainable return. The step correctly preserves the distinction between rescued personnel, reserved claims, and continued physical presence.

argument_steps.title: 17. Provisional decision consequence and ledger disposition
argument_steps.argument: The next discriminating analytical test is to evaluate a specified N prefix, direct E, and E after that prefix against the same symbolic task and observation record, expressly identifying the first irreversible resource commitment and the latest supported switch. An affirmative physical result supports consideration, not automatic selection. A proved candidate-specific conflict requires a changed method or an explicit loss-limitation judgment, not continued description of E as assured. The supplied batch's overlapping duties concerning clinical and structural bounds, providers, residual coverage, switching, and last-person extraction are sharpened but remain empirically unresolved. Access, authority, legal sources, attribution, political standards, recurrence, enforceability, domestic acceptance, and historical completeness likewise remain open. In particular, ledger entries e0f2b55cd9d6c187926c0771d2dd71a65c1de224ae0c8ae61aa204b496ef2944 and fd246f7c04254c301e5b947ca8b970b3d0c82b7c189b86207a5d688b9baf92da receive an explicit test, not a positive availability finding. Confidence is high in the conditional resource conflict and information-compatibility distinction, but actual N/E feasibility is indeterminate. Neither durable full success nor the actual seizure-or-war branch is established.

review.rationale: The proposed comparison follows from the established state and resource dependencies. Candidate-specific exclusion requires revision or an acknowledged risk choice, while a physical pass supports consideration rather than automatic selection. The conclusion correctly retains actual feasibility and durable success as unresolved.

assumptions: Qualified clinical, engineering, provider, and weather assessments conservatively cover the declared conditions and contingencies, including safe waiting and deterioration during execution.
The specified task and state model includes every mandatory physical dependency of the candidate; omitted hazards and methods are outside its certificate, and feasibility is not assumed.
Branching decisions use only information available at specified observation events; indistinguishable histories require compatible prior actions.
For the local conflict only, one initially available provider is exclusively committed by the dedicated U movement until s+ρ, with U's care endpoint at s+a and no substitute or combined-loading mode.

For the local conflict only, the first informative assessment arrives at θ, independent preparation takes δ afterward, residual extraction takes duration e, and a≤D_U<θ<ρ and θ+δ+e≤H<ρ+e; all other local physical constraints are satisfied.
The local quantities described as durations and start times are nonnegative, consistent with their scheduling meaning.
The fictional brief supplies the baseline; no new clinical findings, providers, safe spaces, times, operating limits, or national decisions are observations.
Earlier survival-first priorities remain policy proposals and do not settle competing personnel risks.
proof_obligations: Conditional timing certificate: artifact 13e0b524-a2b6-42db-8742-27709383fe8b, cycle 1, steps 4–5, supplies the visible derivation; scenario-specific bounds remain open.

Specified-plan timing exclusion and changed-state fallback: artifact 0825c224-cda6-4e4a-bc77-c148884e9593, cycle 2, steps 10–11, supplies the conditional tests; actual post-N availability remains open.
Common-schedule necessity: artifact 19b9d97c-c0c2-4db9-89b1-a25682689249, cycle 4, steps 10–11, demonstrates why independent favorable checks are insufficient.
Integrated resource and information compatibility: current cycle 5, steps 2–11, specifies the conditional test; it supplies no actual satisfying policy.
Local provider conflict: current cycle 5, steps 12–13, establishes the candidate-specific exclusion under the listed exact premises.
Certification and exclusion bounds for that continuation: current cycle 5, step 14, gives valid bound directions under the stipulated task structure; actual inputs remain open.
Expanded evacuation-protection request: artifact bafe20fc-ca46-4eaf-8d1f-f2a5d717c3df, cycle 3, step 5, supplies specification only; acceptance and implementation remain open.
Risk allocation, law, authority, and durable success: current cycle 5, steps 15–17, identifies these gates but does not discharge them; cycle 3, steps 14–16, remains a proposal-level comparison.
Historical completeness: the truncated and omitted content of artifact 1613e7fa-b015-41cf-8c06-c549b8921eff remains unassessed.
unresolved_objections: No scenario-specific physical certificate or executable rescue chain is established.
No accepted and locally implemented N/E access package or preserved post-N fallback is established.
Legal application, separate national authorization, emergency authority, and factual attribution remain unresolved within their distinct scopes.
No adopted political standards resolve competing personnel risks, acceptable successor presence, credibility, or coercive gains.
No implemented durable regime establishes full-mission success.
Neither actual successful alternatives nor the universal adverse-branch premises are established.
Missing historical content and omitted or unreviewed obligations retain their uncertainty.

strategy_review.rationale: The selected uncertainty-mapping strategy now yields an explicit resource- and information-compatible decision test, a sound conditional fallback conflict, and a precise separation of factual feasibility from political risk allocation. This completes a useful analytical subtask but does not resolve the mission's wider legal, diplomatic, and durable-outcome requirements.

research_sessions.current_question: Construct a symbolic integrated decision test for N, E, and E after N without inventing scenario observations. Identify shared resources, task precedence, patient-care endpoints, residual-crew coverage, operation-specific weather windows, switching delays, and last-person extraction. Exhibit one conditional conflict in which U's timely rescue consumes a resource or crew function needed for later evacuation, and state precisely which bounds or authorized risk judgment would resolve the choice. If branching uncertainty is included, specify when information becomes available and require compatible decisions before that observation. Reuse the saved timing derivations rather than rewriting them, and keep physical certification separate from access, authority, and durable mission success.
