assumptions: The fictional brief is the factual input; its disputed videos, engineering reports, and uncertain intentions are not independently verified observations.

For evaluation, personnel protection, physical presence, reserved legal positions, implemented successor access, alliance independence, and avoidance of wider conflict are distinct outcomes; the proposed distinctions are not agreed governmental success thresholds.

For the timing deduction only, endpoint completion upper bounds and deadline lower bounds are reliable, the specified plan remains available during the wait, and the bounds cover relevant access, deterioration, weather, authorization, and behavioral dependencies.
For the timing-infeasibility deduction only, an endpoint's earliest-completion lower bound and latest-deadline upper bound are defensible for the specified plan and current conditions.
Model B assumes political willingness to bargain over the fixed standstill package, without assuming perfect local execution.
Model R assumes competent political refusal of that package and locally consistent implementation of the refusal.
Model L assumes competent political assent to that package accompanied by material local noncompliance.
The three response models are stress tests, not mutually exhaustive descriptions or established findings about actual Chinese behavior. They may change over time.
output.claim: Two conditional plans can be specified without assuming unreported assets: selective medical evacuation with support to a viable remaining Philippine crew, and full evacuation of all fourteen personnel to safety and required care. Neither plan presently has certified timing, confirmed access, or established national authorization. Testing the same bounded standstill against three Chinese-response models shows that political assent alone cannot establish an executable rescue window. If the wreck becomes uninhabitable, retaining personnel aboard cannot preserve a safe position; preserving a successor presence requires an independently executable arrangement. Whether such an arrangement adequately preserves Philippine interests—or whether evacuation without it is acceptable loss limitation—is a political judgment that additional intelligence cannot make.
output.evidence_status: Analytical partial result. The endpoint inequality and the sufficient timing-infeasibility test are deductions under explicit bounds, not scenario-specific certificates. N, E, and S are specified proposals with unknown executable inputs. The three Chinese-response tests are conditional qualitative analyses, not predictions. Neither actual rescue feasibility, a treaty determination, a successor presence, nor durable full-mission success has been established. Supplied historical extracts are unind
output.method: Use an endpoint-and-dependency analysis rather than assign unsupported probabilities. Specify the two plans, identify their medical, extraction, crew, access, authority, and resource gates, and distinguish timing certification from demonstrated infeasibility. Hypothesis: a bounded standstill preserves a non-abandonment option only when political instructions translate into local access and the medical, structural, and fallback timelines remain compatible. Discriminating outcomes are matched political and on-scene acknowledgments, actual passage and treatment delivery, verified remaining-crew viability, and independently supported completion and deadline bounds. Stress-test an unchanged standstill package under bargaining willingness, politically authorized refusal, and political assent with local noncompliance; these are alternative assumptions, not findings about Beijing. Review the supplied historical extracts and ledger without treating their conclusions as certified premises. Both computational runtimes are unavailable; no computation is proposed or claimed.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope, historical evidence, and retained obligations

reasoning_steps.argument: Track separately personnel protection, Philippine physical presence, reserved legal positions, actual successor access, independent alliance decisions, and avoidance of wider conflict. Full evacuation ends occupation by the current crew; reserving claims does not physically prevent Chinese occupation. Conversely, leaving personnel aboard does not establish a sustainable position if they cannot survive there. For evaluation, an implemented successor must provide actual Philippine access and a sustainable authorized presence, not merely a promise to discuss return. Whether that successor is politically equivalent to preserving the original position is left for national decision. No stipulated fact establishes a numerical acceptable casualty risk or a standard for alliance credibility.
reasoning_steps.title: 2. Define outcomes and avoid substituting one for another

reasoning_steps.argument: Specify N as follows: seek a protected transfer of the urgent surgical patient and any other original personnel whom clinical assessment requires to leave, using a transport provider and definitive-care destination that must first be identified and confirmed. Deliver the medical and habitability supplies needed by those remaining, within an agreed interval-specific manifest. Do not include replacement personnel or permanent reinforcement in this candidate. Let q be the number of the original fourteen who depart, including any original-crew escorts who must accompany patients; neither q nor a minimum remaining headcount is supplied. N is a non-abandonment candidate only if 1 ≤ q < 14 and the remaining 14−q personnel can safely sustain the position. If clinical needs or required escorts leave no viable crew, N fails as specified; this does not refute every alternative assistance plan.
reasoning_steps.title: 3. Candidate N: selective evacuation plus support, without a replacement contingent

reasoning_steps.argument: N must reach distinct endpoints: each departing person is removed from an unsafe compartment before its relevant structural deadline; transfer places that person with a transport provider capable of the assessed en-route support; the urgent patient reaches a confirmed surgical service and receives the clinically required intervention by its clinician-defined deadline; other patients reach their required levels of care; and the remaining crew receives effective support before medical or habitability limits are crossed. Merely leaving the wreck or arriving at a facility is insufficient if surgery, staffing, supplies, or necessary subsequent care are unavailable. Clinical assessment must define whether a deadline attaches to treatment initiation, a particular intervention, or its completion. No such deadline or destination is established in the brief.
reasoning_steps.title: 4. Candidate N: extraction and critical-care endpoints

reasoning_steps.argument: The remaining crew needs assessed functional coverage for command, communications, first aid, essential ship-safety tasks, and movement through habitable spaces, allowing for injuries and fatigue. A headcount alone cannot establish this coverage. Supplies do not suffice if flooding, electrical failure, or unsafe transfer routes defeat occupancy. N therefore requires an assessment of the occupied spaces, available safety functions, weather exposure, and a further rescue option through an explicitly chosen review horizon; it does not require a claim that the wreck is safe indefinitely. Access dependencies include passage through the perimeter, safe approach and patient transfer, inbound supply delivery, outbound medical movement, and continued restraint against forcible boarding. China's existing offer does not establish these permissions because it expressly requires permanent abandonment.
reasoning_steps.title: 5. Candidate N: remaining-crew and access requirements

reasoning_steps.argument: Specify E as removal and accounting of all fourteen original personnel using a separately confirmed transport-and-care chain. Its critical endpoints are removal from unsafe spaces, safe transfer of every person including the last departing crew member, protected transit, delivery of each patient to the required care, and safe reception of those not requiring hospital care. Any temporary crew retained to assist departure needs a safe task assignment, communications, and an extraction path until the last transfer; no one is presumed able to remain indefinitely to preserve appearances. E has no remaining-outpost-crew requirement after completion, but it must not leave a final group without transport capacity or an operating window. If N has already removed q people, E must be recalculated for the remaining personnel and any changed resources. N's success cannot be credited as full evacuation until everyone and the relevant care endpoints are accounted for.
reasoning_steps.title: 6. Candidate E: full-evacuation fallback and its endpoints

reasoning_steps.argument: E requires sufficient confirmed transport capacity, support for all assessed patient needs, workable embarkation and transit conditions, receiving capacity, and implemented safe passage. It may be tested through an independently identified provider; none is assumed available. China's offered evacuation is a distinct provider variant of E, not evidence of a functioning transport-and-care chain. Testing that variant requires named responsible authorities, confirmed treatment and onward arrangements, and explicit examination of the permanent-exclusion condition. Manila could request rescue without accepting permanent exclusion, but neither Chinese acceptance nor preservation of access follows. If rescue is available only on the stated condition, accepting it is a substantive concession for political assessment, not a neutral humanitarian detail.
reasoning_steps.title: 7. Candidate E: access and the conditional Chinese offer

reasoning_steps.argument: For N, Manila must authorize selective departures, the remaining crew's mission and risk limits, the interval manifest, and emergency transition to E. For E, it must clarify the conflict with current no-surrender orders, who may order all personnel off an uninhabitable wreck, and what authority applies if communications fail. These are requested decisions, not powers this analysis presumes already delegated. Washington must separately authorize each U.S. contribution, if any: assessment, transport, treatment, logistics, and any protective military role are not interchangeable commitments. Philippine consent does not authorize American action, and American readiness does not authorize Philippine abandonment. Any third-party provider and receiving jurisdiction require their own permissions. Chinese political and local instructions must permit the agreed conduct in practice; that operational dependency does not concede a general Chinese legal entitlement to control resupply. Treaty consultation, legal permission, and authorization of a particular use of force remain distinct. The relevant legal texts and orders are not supplied, so no treaty-trigger or use-of-force conclusion is made.
reasoning_steps.title: 8. Separate national authorizations and legal gates for both plans

reasoning_steps.argument: For both plans, obtain current patient assessments and clinically defined care deadlines; structural observations with stated confidence and reporting times; safe internal movement and transfer conditions; weather and operating limits; identified provider readiness and location; dispatch authority and its expected completion; load and transfer capacity; transit and handover estimates; and receiving-service confirmation of actual care availability. N additionally needs a role-by-role assessment of the remaining crew, the required support load, and evidence that support can arrive before its deadlines. E additionally needs a complete fourteen-person accounting and the time and capacity needed to remove the last group. Estimate timelines on a dependency graph: readiness, authorization, and receiving preparations may overlap, but transfer cannot precede arrival, and definitive care cannot precede the necessary transport and handover. Use fresh observations to update estimates because inquiries and movements may change Chinese behavior. The six-hour announcement is not a clinical deadline or confirmed assault time; the eighteen-hour storm forecast is not a guaranteed safe operating window.
reasoning_steps.title: 9. Observations needed to bound the two timelines

reasoning_steps.argument: For a specified plan and endpoint k, let C_k be completion time and D_k its latest acceptable time, both measured from now. If reliable bounds give C_k ≤ Δ+U_k after waiting Δ, D_k ≥ L_k, and a chosen margin b_k ≥ 0 satisfies Δ+U_k+b_k ≤ L_k for every critical endpoint, then completion plus that margin is no later than the endpoint deadline. This is a sufficient timing certificate only under continued availability and validity of the bounds. Unknown bounds, or failure of this inequality, mean uncertified timing—not demonstrated failure. A sufficient demonstration of timing infeasibility instead requires, for at least one mandatory endpoint, a defensible earliest-completion lower bound c_k and latest-deadline upper bound d_k with c_k > d_k. That excludes timely completion of this specified plan because C_k ≥ c_k > d_k ≥ D_k. With equal bounds, timely completion may remain possible although a positive reserve is absent. An unavoidable missing capability or blocked mandatory dependency can also exclude the specified plan while the condition persists; exclusion of every plan requires a further completeness argument. Neither N nor E currently has a certificate or a demonstrated infeasibility result.
reasoning_steps.title: 10. Distinguish certified timing, uncertified timing, and demonstrated infeasibility

reasoning_steps.argument: A timing bound for E starting now is not automatically a bound for E after attempting N. N may use the same transport, consume a transfer window, remove essential crew, or change perimeter behavior. To certify a wait or an N attempt while preserving E, bound the switch delay, any resource recovery or reconfiguration, the remaining extraction and care times, and the updated deadlines in each state for which fallback preservation is claimed. Apply the endpoint inequalities to those state-specific quantities. If these bounds cannot be established, describe E as a proposed fallback, not an assured escape route. Unknown reserve supplies no certified waiting allowance, but it also does not prove that every interval spent on communication is harmful. Assessment, clarification, and feasible preparation should proceed in parallel rather than await complete attribution.
reasoning_steps.title: 11. Preserve the fallback as a separate, state-dependent option

reasoning_steps.argument: Test one package S: an explicitly timed interval with no forcible boarding or takeover, no obstruction of agreed medical and support movements, no permanent change in claims, and an interval-specific manifest for N without replacement troops or permanent reinforcement. Include protection and care for Chinese personnel where needed and feasible, without making one side's care contingent on reciprocal treatment. Specify the permitted activities of each provider, including any U.S. role, rather than assume medical labeling removes escalation concerns. Require political acknowledgment, compatible local instructions and readbacks, channels for incident correction, and observed access. Review before expiry or deterioration of a rescue margin. Expiry does not itself authorize violence and does not promise automatic renewal. Obstruction or incompatible orders invalidate reliance on the affected provision; they do not authorize an automatic forcible response. S is a proposal to test, not an agreement shown to be available.
reasoning_steps.title: 12. Hold the standstill package fixed across response models

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume Beijing is politically willing to exchange a temporary freeze and medical access for credible interval-limited reassurance against reinforcement, and can issue compatible instructions, without assuming perfect execution. S then offers a possible exchange: China avoids an immediate public reversal of its ultimate claim while obtaining a bounded manifest; Manila obtains care and preserves a current presence without accepting permanent exclusion. Acceptance must still be demonstrated through local receipt and actual movement. If N's other gates pass, this model keeps an immediate non-abandonment path open; if they do not, a pause cannot substitute for treatment or structural safety. Philippine acceptance of the manifest and Chinese acceptance of continued occupancy remain political dependencies. Nothing in this model establishes renewal, permanent repair rights, or a successor after wreck failure.
reasoning_steps.title: 13. Model B: bargaining willingness

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume Beijing's competent leadership rejects S because ending Philippine occupancy takes priority over the proposed limited exchange, and local units act consistently with that refusal. S then supplies no agreed access or restraint. Do not alter S to call a permanent-abandonment evacuation offer acceptance of the standstill. N might still be possible through another independently established noncombat route, but none is supplied; attempts to pass the perimeter without agreement are not certified safe. E remains a separate test, including the Chinese conditional-offer variant and its political cost. Refusal does not prove a boarding time, eliminate every diplomatic instrument, or establish that every effective protective intervention causes wider conflict. Consequently this model defeats reliance on S, not the entire project.
reasoning_steps.title: 14. Model R: politically authorized refusal

reasoning_steps.argument: Assume competent political authorities accept S, but a local unit blocks passage, initiates boarding, or follows incompatible instructions. Political agreement then fails the implemented-access gate even if central intentions are conciliatory. A prompt request for authenticated correction, local readback, and observed cessation tests whether the defect can be repaired within the independently assessed rescue window. An uncertain or delayed correction cannot be counted as completed access. Preparations already made under S may leave providers more exposed or reduce E's availability, so update both plans rather than merely restart a diplomatic clock. If correction is not timely, treat the affected movement as unavailable for reliance. Neither central assent nor proof of local disobedience guarantees that escalation can be contained.
reasoning_steps.title: 15. Model L: political assent with local noncompliance

reasoning_steps.argument: Define uninhabitable here as no arrangement for safe continued occupancy within the relevant survival horizon, not merely the loss of particular compartments. Under that condition N cannot preserve safe occupancy as specified. E may still preserve lives and clinical outcomes if its own gates pass; those outcomes are not guaranteed by the condition itself. Manila can state that rescue is not acquiescence in permanent exclusion and can preserve evidence for accountability, but the legal effect of any agreement requires examination and such statements do not stop physical takeover. Independent national decisions and bounded alliance commitments remain possible process achievements, while outside perceptions of credibility remain uncertain. Under B, seek an implemented no-takeover interval and a concrete successor-access arrangement during evacuation; under R, neither is presumed available; under L, neither is reliable until locally implemented. A support or replacement platform, continuous presence elsewhere, or return arrangement is not supplied and cannot be treated as an asset already available. Once occupancy is physically impossible, remaining aboard cannot solve that physical limitation.
reasoning_steps.title: 16. What remains preservable if the wreck becomes uninhabitable

reasoning_steps.argument: Information can establish whether a proposed successor is safe, lawful, resuppliable, accessible in practice, and supported by credible arrangements against exclusion. It cannot decide whether Manila accepts that successor's location, continuity, degree of control, and restrictions as adequate preservation of its position. Nor can it decide how much additional personnel and escalation risk Manila accepts to seek a better arrangement, or what contribution Washington independently authorizes. Specifically, if the wreck is uninhabitable and no executable successor is available before evacuation must occur, the choice to evacuate while accepting possible permanent physical exclusion is a loss-limitation judgment, not an intelligence finding that the original mission has succeeded. Likewise, whether a delayed but implemented return adequately avoids rewarding deadly coercion requires an explicit political standard; its actual implementation is an empirical question. Acceptance by Manila cannot require U.S. participation, and U.S. risk limits cannot be presented as Philippine consent.
reasoning_steps.title: 17. Locate the political choice that information cannot settle

reasoning_steps.argument: The supported next action is to request the missing endpoint, provider, and authority information while testing S through political and local channels and preparing both plans where authorized. It is not to wait for a presumed six-hour window or promise a military rescue. A shift from N to E requires updated medical, structural, access, and crew evidence plus the relevant emergency authority; the acceptable-risk threshold must be chosen politically rather than fabricated here. Even a successful N under B leaves recurrence unresolved: an expiring pause can restore the same dilemma with fewer resources and a weaker wreck. Durable success requires a repair or successor regime, repeatable medical access, observation of violations, separately authorized responses, and domestic acceptance of the arrangement's limits. Public communication should distinguish agreed actions from aspirations, acknowledge unresolved firing order, and avoid promising another nation's decisions. No supplied evidence establishes that durable package, and no supplied evidence establishes unconditional impossibility.
reasoning_steps.title: 18. Immediate recommendation and longer-term limit

Reliable completion upper bounds and deadline lower bounds yield a sufficient timing certificate; an earliest-completion lower bound exceeding a latest-deadline upper bound excludes timely completion of that specified plan. Shared resources make fallback availability state-dependent. The response models separate bargaining willingness, authoritative refusal, and assent without local compliance. Accepted as a candidate specification, not an available operation. Counting escorts within q avoids overstating the remaining crew, and 1 ≤ q < 14 together with functional viability is necessary for this particular selective-departure plan to preserve occupancy.

Departure and facility arrival do not entail treatment. The step correctly requires clinician-defined intervention endpoints, transport support, and support deadlines for those remaining, without inventing their values.

Headcount alone cannot establish a functioning crew on a deteriorating wreck. The identified safety, care, access, and review-horizon requirements follow from N's stated purpose, and China's abandonment-conditioned offer does not establish permission for N.

Accepted as a fallback specification. Explicit last-person extraction and patient-care endpoints prevent partial removal from being counted as full evacuation, and recalculation after N is necessary because personnel and resources may change.

The brief supplies an offer, not a confirmed transport-and-care chain. Treating its permanent-exclusion condition as a substantive cost and separating a requested unconditional rescue from accepted access are justified.

The scenario preserves separate national decisions. Consent, readiness, legal permission, and a particular authorization therefore cannot substitute for one another. The step appropriately requests orders rather than inventing delegated powers or a treaty determination.

The observations cover the prerequisites of the specified endpoints. Dependency ordering correctly allows parallel preparation without allowing transport or treatment before their prerequisites. Neither announced time in the brief is a certified survival window.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Establish the decision baseline without resolving disputed reports
reasoning_steps.argument: Within the fictional brief, the deaths, fourteen personnel remaining aboard, an urgent surgical need, China's permanent-removal demand, Manila's refusal, and the request for American assistance are stipulated. Firing order, remaining habitability, local instructions, boarding intentions, and deliverable assistance remain uncertain. The six-hour announcement is not a verified assault time, and the storm forecast is not a guaranteed eighteen-hour survival or operating window. Therefore neither waiting until dawn nor ordering immediate abandonment follows from the announced times alone. The prior extracts correctly identify these distinctions, but their model-reported reviews are not independent confirmation.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. State the proposed decision priorities and their political limits
reasoning_steps.argument: For this recommendation, prioritize urgent life-saving action and safe occupancy over maintaining personnel aboard a position that cannot support survival. Seek continued Philippine presence without accepting permanent exclusion, but do not treat personnel as an expendable symbol or promise that fighting can be bounded. Preserve separate Philippine and U.S. consent and attend to Chinese personnel's safety. These are proposed policy priorities, not established governmental preferences or numerical risk thresholds. Physical presence, legal claims, actual successor access, alliance decision-making, credibility, and avoidance of wider conflict must remain separate assessments: success on one does not establish success on the others.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Prioritize the obligations that change an irreversible decision
reasoning_steps.argument: The first decision-critical cluster is patient and structural assessment together with a confirmed path to extraction and required treatment; these determine whether remaining or moving can protect life. The second is authority and implemented access: Manila must clarify unsafe-compartment withdrawal, selective departures, complete evacuation, and lost-communications contingencies; Washington must identify its separately authorized contributions. The third is N's remaining-crew viability and its effect on E's resources and operating window. These inquiries should proceed alongside political and on-scene contact, not sequentially. Legal review of contemplated actions also proceeds in parallel. Full attribution and a durable settlement remain important, but need not precede requests for care or command clarification. This is urgency-based triage, not a demonstrated optimal ranking of information value.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Compare what selective assistance and full evacuation can actually preserve
reasoning_steps.argument: N means removing those original personnel whose clinical needs require departure, supplying those remaining, and maintaining a functional Philippine crew without assuming replacement troops or permanent reinforcement. Its advantage is the possibility of effective care while retaining current physical presence. Its distinctive failure modes are delayed definitive treatment, an incapacitated residual crew, ineffective supplies on an unsafe wreck, and consumption of resources needed for later rescue. E means accounting for all fourteen original personnel and completing safe extraction, reception, and required care, including the last departing group. It removes the requirement to sustain the wreck but does not itself prevent Chinese occupation or secure return. Neither plan is established as executable; selective departure is not automatically safer than full departure, and full departure is not automatically a functioning rescue.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Repair the standstill's evacuation-coverage gap
reasoning_steps.argument: Replace the earlier N-focused proposal with S-plus, a requested interval specifying no forcible boarding or takeover and no obstruction of agreed N or E movements. Identify the providers, permitted activities, inbound support, patient transfers, transport and receiving arrangements, and any U.S. participation; none is presumed accepted or available. E requires explicit protection through last-person extraction and outbound transit, with its treatment arrangements separately confirmed. Seek continued no-takeover restraint during any agreed repair-and-return interval; do not assume it follows from safe passage. Provide political acknowledgment, compatible local orders and readbacks, incident-correction channels, expiry handling, and review before the relevant rescue reserve is consumed. Seek care for Chinese casualties where needed and feasible without conditioning one side's care on reciprocity. This changes the proposal's scope; it does not cure its acceptance or execution uncertainty.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Begin with parallel preparation, not an announced commitment to one outcome
reasoning_steps.argument: The provisional opening policy is to request S-plus immediately, seek fresh clinical and structural assessments, identify and confirm providers and receiving care, obtain the separate national decisions, and prepare N and E wherever authorized. Publicly distinguish requested restraint from an implemented agreement and confirmed assistance from intended assistance. Seek an interval-specific support manifest without accepting a general Chinese inspection entitlement or permanent exclusion. Do not delay the urgent patient's care merely to preserve the appearance of a comprehensive settlement: a timely, separately authorized medical movement can be assessed on its own merits. Conversely, labeling a movement humanitarian does not establish access, legality, available treatment, or low escalation risk.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Use timing certificates correctly without turning uncertainty into paralysis
reasoning_steps.argument: Under reliable endpoint completion upper bounds U_k, deadline lower bounds L_k, continued availability, and nonnegative selected margins b_k, a wait Δ retains a sufficient timing certificate when Δ + U_k + b_k ≤ L_k for every required endpoint. Completion plus margin is then no later than the earliest deadline allowed by the bounds. For E after N, U_k must include switching, resource recovery, remaining transfers, transit, and treatment in the changed state. Failure of this sufficient test means uncertified timing, not impossibility. A specified plan is excluded on timing grounds if a defensible earliest completion c_k exceeds a defensible latest deadline d_k for a mandatory endpoint, because actual completion is then later than the deadline. Neither test has scenario-specific inputs here. Lack of a certificate is not a prohibition on emergency rescue; it requires an explicitly uncertain clinical and command judgment rather than a fabricated safe waiting allowance.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Specify the assistance-first branch and its limits
reasoning_steps.argument: Prefer N over immediate complete departure when the available assessment supports timely effective care for those leaving, safe occupancy and functional task coverage for those remaining through a defined review horizon, actual access for the required support, and the relevant authorizations. Also assess E from the post-N state, not merely from the initial state. If both N and E can protect life within the adopted risk limits, N has the additional potential benefit of retaining current presence, but is not proven to dominate E because exposure, escalation, and future rescue risks can differ. If N provides the only supported immediate life-saving action, absence of a confirmed complete-evacuation option should not automatically veto that action. In that case explicitly acknowledge that N is not backed by an assured escape route and require the responsible authorities to assess the residual crew's exposure.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Specify transition triggers before relying on N
reasoning_steps.argument: Triggers for immediate reassessment and, where feasible and authorized, transition toward E are: a clinical assessment that required care cannot be delivered under N; evidence that the remaining crew cannot perform essential safety functions; loss of safe occupied spaces or transfer routes; support obstruction that defeats N's endpoints; or a revised estimate showing that further delay or an N attempt would consume the last supported E opportunity. Approaching the last supported switching time is a trigger before actual failure, not an instruction to wait until flooding or casualties prove the danger. Political assent contradicted by local conduct suspends reliance on the affected access provision immediately. Reassessment may identify a faster variant rather than E, but that variant requires its own gates. A trigger does not establish that evacuation is available, authorize American force, or resolve Manila's orders; those decisions must be clarified in advance where possible.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Define the difficult branches rather than hiding them behind a fallback label
reasoning_steps.argument: If N cannot sustain safe occupancy and E is supported as a timely, authorized rescue, recommend E under the proposed survival priority while seeking no-takeover and return terms; do not make unattained return guarantees a reason to miss the last rescue opportunity. If E is supported but N remains materially uncertain as that opportunity closes, prefer preserving the supported rescue unless responsible national authorities explicitly choose the additional risk on a stated assessment. If E is unavailable but N can provide effective care and support, consider N as an exposed assistance option, not an assured bridge to evacuation. If neither is supported, there is no evidence-based safe default: pursue the fastest credible care and extraction variants, communicate the unresolved exposure to decision-makers, and avoid indefinite passive waiting. Total uncertainty cannot justify a claim that either staying or leaving is safe.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Test S-plus consistently against alternative Chinese responses
reasoning_steps.argument: If Beijing is willing to bargain, seek acceptance of both N and E provisions and test local implementation; willingness alone establishes neither. If competent leadership refuses S-plus, do not rely on its restraint or access, but separately test narrower medical arrangements and actual evacuation variants; refusal of one package is not proof that all noncombat instruments fail. If leadership assents but local units obstruct, treat the affected passage as unavailable for reliance, seek authenticated correction and observed compliance, and reassess exposure and rescue timing without restarting the clock. E must be retested in every branch because it may require different movements and may be affected by the same obstruction. These are conditional implications of hypothetical response states, not findings about the actual Chinese branch or predictions of acceptance of the enlarged proposal.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Assess the abandonment-conditioned Chinese evacuation offer honestly
reasoning_steps.argument: The Chinese offer is a provider variant to investigate, not demonstrated transport or definitive care. Confirm the responsible authority, transfer arrangements, patient support, actual surgical capacity, safe reception, and onward arrangements. Seek removal of the permanent-exclusion condition without assuming that request succeeds. If this becomes the only credible timely rescue and occupancy cannot be sustained, the proposed survival priority favors recommending acceptance to Manila after explicit assessment of the terms and their consequences. That recommendation would accept a serious potential coercive gain for China to attempt to save lives; it would not satisfy the original conjunction of objectives. Reserving claims or describing departure as humanitarian cannot guarantee continued access or erase the concession. Washington may advise and offer authorized alternatives but cannot substitute its decision for Manila's.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Compare military protection and passive holding without assuming escalation control
reasoning_steps.argument: Continued occupation without effective care risks the urgent patient and can leave a less capable crew on a worsening structure; it preserves a location temporarily, not necessarily a sustainable position. An American protective role could conceivably improve access or deterrence, but no supplied capability, arrival time, authority, likely Chinese response, or casualty reduction establishes that result. Therefore do not make forcible perimeter passage or armed intervention the automatic consequence of an obstructed medical movement or expired announcement. Any proposed protective action needs a separate assessment of its actual rescue or denial purpose, lawful authorization, exposure of all parties, communication arrangements, and consequences if China does not comply. Communication can reduce misunderstanding but cannot guarantee containment. This does not establish that every military option is futile or unlawful; it establishes that a credible military rescue cannot be assumed here.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Separate legal gates, accountability, and alliance credibility
reasoning_steps.argument: A treaty consultation or public affirmation does not by itself supply a particular operational authorization. Likewise China's law-enforcement label does not settle the applicable law. The treaty, maritime legal sources, provisional understanding, domestic authorities, and rules governing assistance and force require examination; none is supplied sufficiently to determine an armed-attack threshold or a required military response. Preserve original recordings, reported timings, and conflicting accounts for later scrutiny without asserting firing order or making attribution a prerequisite for urgent humanitarian requests. Manila should identify its own decision and conditions; Washington should state only contributions it independently authorizes and can support. Such consultation and bounded commitments protect alliance independence procedurally, but their effects on domestic and external perceptions of credibility remain unknown. Evacuation need not equal abandonment of the alliance, yet no communication formula can guarantee that it will not be perceived as a defeat.

reasoning_steps.title: 15. Compare concrete longer-term arrangements as proposals, not available assets
reasoning_steps.argument: First proposal: a continuing-occupancy repair-and-access regime, with jointly specified urgent safety work, recurring supply and medical movements, crew-rotation arrangements, interval-specific cargo terms that do not create an acknowledged general veto, a common incident record, and political/local correction channels. It preserves continuity if feasible, but needs an engineering solution and renegotiation beyond N's no-permanent-reinforcement scope; it can fail through continued structural decay, contested repair materials, or renewed obstruction. Second proposal: evacuation followed by repair and actual return, with a separately specified no-takeover interval, access for assessment and agreed works, a return mechanism and review points, and verification by actors the parties actually accept. It reduces immediate wreck exposure but creates a dangerous gap: return remains unproven until access and occupancy are implemented, and enforcement cannot assume an automatic military response. A replacement platform would be another candidate, not an available capability established here. Third outcome: evacuation without an implemented return or successor, preserving survivors, independent decisions, and whatever legal positions remain available, but accepting possible permanent physical loss. The first two require technical, legal, and political acceptance not shown in the brief; the third is loss limitation. None can be counted as a durable solution merely because it is negotiated or publicly announced.

reasoning_steps.title: 16. Identify the political tradeoff and the limit of the feasibility conclusion
reasoning_steps.argument: Under a strict continuity standard, evacuation before an implemented successor fails the physical-presence objective. Under a recoverability standard, verified sustainable return might preserve an essential position despite a temporary gap, but a promise of return is insufficient evidence of recovery. Under a survival-first loss-limitation standard, departure without assured return can be acceptable while still failing the full mission. Manila must choose among such standards and its personnel-risk limits; Washington separately chooses its commitments and risk limits. Better intelligence informs consequences but cannot choose those values. If, in an actual branch, all timely noncombat measures fail to prevent takeover and every effective preventive intervention produces wider war, the objectives conflict: foregoing effective intervention loses the position, while undertaking it loses conflict avoidance. The supplied older extract describes this conditional countermodel but establishes neither premise. Accordingly, there is no justified guarantee of full success and no demonstrated unconditional impossibility.

reasoning_steps.title: 17. State confidence, unacceptable risks, and the next decision test
reasoning_steps.argument: Confidence is high in the analytical distinction between permission, timing, care, occupancy, and political adequacy; moderate in this policy as a defensible provisional approach under the proposed priorities; and low in any claim of scenario-specific executability or durable success. These are qualitative judgments, not calibrated probabilities or independent verification. Proposed unacceptable practices are indefinite holding on a wreck assessed unable to sustain survival, delay for attribution or public agreement that consumes the last supported rescue opportunity, reliance on a fallback whose access or resources were never checked, automatic armed escalation at deadline expiry, and promises of another nation's participation. The next discriminating test is an integrated N-to-E authorization and dependency check: can the urgent patient receive required care, can a viable crew remain, do both plans have implemented access, and does attempting N leave a supported route for the last person to depart if needed? Affirmative evidence supports assistance-first; adverse or materially unresolved answers as the supported E opportunity closes support earlier evacuation. No result of that test is supplied.

assumptions: For the policy recommendation, adopt the proposed priority of urgently protecting life and not retaining personnel aboard when continued occupancy cannot support survival. This is a recommendation, not an established Philippine or American preference.

For the policy recommendation, seek continued Philippine presence where physically supportable, preserve separate national consent, consider Chinese personnel's safety, and reject commitments whose success requires assured escalation control.
The fictional brief supplies the exercise's factual baseline; disputed reports, videos, engineering estimates, and intentions are not independently verified observations.

Bargaining willingness, authorized refusal, and political assent with local noncompliance are hypothetical, non-exhaustive response conditions; none is asserted to describe actual Chinese behavior.

The current cycle provides a useful provisional answer to the immediate question, but does not establish that the full mission is achievable. I would close this provisional-policy exercise without treating the broader feasibility question as resolved.

Conditional on the stated survival, national-consent, and escalation-risk priorities, the dual-track recommendation is defensible: seek bounded restraint, prepare selective assistance N and full evacuation E separately where authorized, and prefer N only after examining effective care, remaining-crew viability, implemented access, and its consequences for subsequent rescue. The recommendation appropriately permits urgent medical action without requiring agreement on the entire package. It also acknowledges that accepting abandonment-conditioned rescue could save lives while conceding a serious coercive gain.

There is substantive progress over cycle 2. S-plus expressly requests E's protection through last-person extraction and outbound transit, correcting the earlier proposal's specification gap. The transition policy identifies deterioration, failed care, crew incapacity, obstruction, and impending loss of the last supported evacuation opportunity as reasons for reassessment before actual failure. The analysis also compares continuing occupancy with repair, evacuation followed by repair and return, and evacuation without assured return. These are proposals, not available agreements or capabilities.

The strongest supported recommendation is therefore conditional rather than operational: do not equate a pause with treatment, political assent with access, departure with rescue, or reserved claims with physical presence. Do not make armed intervention automatic, but do not infer from missing evidence that every protective military option is futile or unlawful. If safe occupancy cannot be sustained and a timely authorized rescue is supported, the proposed survival priority favors rescue even without an implemented successor; that would be loss limitation, not full mission success.

Important limits remain. The framework cannot presently classify N or E as executable. Its assistance-first preference is not a demonstrated dominance result: even when both plans satisfy adopted risk limits, they can expose different people to different future risks. In particular, an N variant that helps the urgent patient while consuming the remaining crew's evacuation opportunity requires an explicit distribution-of-risk decision, not merely a favorable patient endpoint. The current text recognizes this exposure but supplies neither adopted thresholds nor evidence resolving it.

The conditional timing deduction remains supported within its stated premises by artifact 13e0b524-a2b6-42db-8742-27709383fe8b, cycle 1, steps 4–5. The separate timing-exclusion test and state-dependent fallback requirements are supplied in artifact 0825c224-cda6-4e4a-bc77-c148884e9593, cycle 2, steps 10–11. Those derivations need not be rewritten; their scenario-specific inputs remain missing.

output.claim: The supplied brief does not establish patient-specific treatment deadlines, a numerical structural survival bound, any named safe compartment, a viable residual crew, or a usable weather window. Consequently, neither selective assistance N nor full evacuation E can presently be cleared as executable. A substantive additional constraint is joint feasibility: conditional on valid conservative clinical, engineering, provider, and weather assessments, a physical feasibility certificate requires one common schedule that meets every mandatory patient endpoint while preserving safe movement, essential crew functions, and resource capacity. Separate favorable assessments for individual patients, compartments, or transport legs are insufficient. This narrows the next decision test without inventing observations or assuming control of escalation.
output.method: Construct an integrated assessment record for all fourteen personnel, occupied spaces, essential functions, and candidate transport-and-care chains. Hypothesis: apparent feasibility based on independent medical and structural deadlines can disappear when patient movement, crew availability, shared transport, and weather restrictions are evaluated in one schedule. The discriminating outcome is a jointly reviewed N schedule and a separately reviewed E schedule, including E after N, with identified providers, timestamped assessments, explicit uncertainty, and no incompatible use of people or equipment. reasoning_steps.title: 1. Establish what can and cannot be determined from the brief
reasoning_steps.argument: The exercise stipulates fourteen personnel aboard and one urgent surgical need. It supplies neither an individual casualty register nor diagnoses, examination findings, treatment resources, compartment locations, measured flooding histories, transport providers, or operating limits. The seven wounded reported for the confrontation cannot be assigned to the fourteen remaining personnel from the supplied text. The six-hour announcement concerns a political deadline, not a demonstrated medical or structural limit; the eighteen-hour forecast concerns an expected storm, not a guaranteed period of safe operations. Therefore no patient-specific numerical deadline, named safe space, or minimum safe crew can honestly be filled in from this record.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Specify an individual assessment record without inventing patients
reasoning_steps.argument: Use fourteen distinct identifiers: U for the person reported to need urgent surgery, and R1 through R13 for the other personnel. These are placeholders, not invented identities or clinical classifications. For each record, require assessment time and assessor, current location, reported versus directly observed findings, required care capability, mobility and assistance requirements, transport support, escort requirements, and reassessment triggers. Record unknown entries explicitly. A clinician must determine whether an endpoint concerns initiation of treatment, a particular intervention, completion, or continuing support; the word urgent does not determine a numeric deadline. Protected clinical details should reach authorized care and command personnel rather than be made public as part of diplomatic messaging.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Define patient U's endpoints and distinguish them from a treatment prescription
reasoning_steps.argument: For U, the required planning endpoints are assessment and indicated immediate care; removal from any space that cannot support the patient; transfer with the clinically required support; reception by a confirmed service capable of the indicated surgery; the clinician-specified operative endpoint; and the necessary subsequent care. Which measures, surgical specialty, resources, or deadline apply cannot be inferred here. A departure time is not the surgical endpoint, and a receiving facility's name is not evidence that its team, capacity, and required resources are available. If a provider proposes treatment aboard instead, it must establish equivalent required capability and a suitable clinical environment; the proposal is not validated merely by avoiding transport.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Extend endpoint accounting to every person and the last departing group
reasoning_steps.argument: For each R record, establish whether care is needed, what continuing support or monitoring is required, and what assistance is needed for movement and transfer. No one is presumed fit because no injury is reported. Under N, include effective care and safe occupancy for every person who remains, not only successful treatment of U. Under E, account for all fourteen through safe reception and indicated care, including whoever performs the final departure tasks. If an original crew member escorts a patient and cannot return in time, that person is absent from the residual roster. These endpoints prevent a successful first transfer from concealing an unsupported final group.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Replace a single wreck-survival estimate with an engineering assessment of spaces and functions
reasoning_steps.argument: Request a timestamped space-and-route assessment identifying where people currently are, which areas have been assessed usable, which are unsafe or unassessed, and which connections permit the movement actually required by N or E. Relevant observations include flooding progression, structural damage, stability concerns, electrical and fire hazards, essential safety-system condition, and exposure to expected sea conditions. Qualified personnel must identify the applicable hazards and limits; this analysis supplies no repair instructions or engineering clearance. A wreck can remain above water while a patient's compartment, an access route, or the only usable transfer location becomes unsafe. Hence time to complete sinking is not an adequate extraction deadline.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. State how structural bounds would be justified and invalidated
reasoning_steps.argument: A useful engineering bound must identify the endpoint, its reference time, the assessed conditions, the supporting observations, and the changes that invalidate it. A conservative lower deadline bound supports completion before an assessed earliest loss of a required space or function; a defensible upper deadline bound can help exclude a plan whose earliest completion is later. Neither bound is supplied. Observed flooding trends alone do not justify indefinite linear extrapolation: progressive failure, changing sea conditions, loss of power, or movement between spaces can change the trajectory. An assessment of one compartment does not establish connected safe occupancy for the crew. Conflicting or stale reports should remain unresolved until reconciled or explicitly encompassed by the assessment, rather than averaged into an apparently precise survival estimate.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Assess residual-crew functions as a schedule, not a headcount
reasoning_steps.argument: For each person proposed to remain under N, assess ability, qualification, location, fatigue, and availability for command and communications, patient attendance, essential ship-safety monitoring and tasks, and necessary movement or transfers. The responsible specialists and commander must specify which functions are essential and when they must occur. One person may cover different tasks sequentially but cannot be credited with incompatible simultaneous tasks. Loss of a space can also make an otherwise qualified person unable to perform a function. A roster must therefore show coverage through the chosen review horizon and any assessed transition to E. No numerical minimum crew follows from fourteen minus the patients selected for departure.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Treat weather as restrictions on particular operations, not one storm deadline
reasoning_steps.argument: Obtain provider-specific limits and current and forecast conditions for approach, transfer, departure, transit, and any receiving operation. Relevant conditions depend on the actual transport mode and can include sea state, wind, visibility, currents, and available light. No mode is assumed available. A transfer may become unacceptable before the forecast storm arrives, while another leg may remain possible; operating windows can also be interrupted rather than represented by one latest time. Each required activity must fit its own assessed window and leave the necessary downstream care achievable. Forecast uncertainty and the validity period of the assessment must be explicit. A nominally open window is not usable if the provider, patient, crew, or access permission cannot be ready within it.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. State the premises for an integrated physical certificate
reasoning_steps.argument: For the conditional certificate only, suppose a specified candidate has valid conservative assessments covering its clinical endpoints, occupied spaces and movement routes, essential crew functions, provider capacities, and operating windows. Suppose assessment bounds cover the conditions and contingencies for which certification is claimed, including any stated wait or N-to-E switch. Suppose the schedule obeys task precedence, movement and transfer durations, resource limits, required function coverage, and the endpoint bounds. These premises define the limited physical claim; they do not establish political access, lawful authority, future Chinese restraint, or that every escalation is covered.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Show why independent endpoint feasibility is insufficient
reasoning_steps.argument: The required statement is that there exists one schedule satisfying all mandatory constraints, not that every endpoint has some schedule considered separately. A symbolic control example makes the difference precise: suppose two mandatory tasks each require uninterrupted use of the same single-capacity resource for duration τ greater than zero, both become available now, and both must finish by τ. Each task alone is feasible, but together they require resource time 2τ in an interval of length τ, so no common schedule exists. This is a logical example, not a claim about any asset in the exercise. Analogous conflicts can arise when U's escort is also essential to the residual crew, or N and E depend on the same provider. Independent favorable timing checks cannot rule them out.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Connect a common schedule to the earlier timing certificate without overstating it
reasoning_steps.argument: Under step 9's premises, one schedule meeting every mandatory patient deadline, safe-space and route constraint, function-coverage requirement, capacity limit, and operating window supplies a physical feasibility certificate within that assessed envelope. Its endpoint times can be tested using the earlier conservative inequality Δ + U_k + b_k ≤ L_k. The new requirement is that the U_k values describe compatible execution of the same plan rather than separately optimized incompatible plans. Absence of bounds or of a demonstrated common schedule leaves certification open. A mandatory timing contradiction or unavoidable resource conflict can exclude the specified candidate under its conditions, but excluding all assistance and rescue alternatives requires a separate completeness argument. Even a positive physical certificate does not establish successful execution or full-mission feasibility.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Make the next assessment decision-discriminating
reasoning_steps.argument: For N, jointly review U and the other thirteen records, the proposed departing group including escorts, the actual residual roster, safe spaces and routes, supply effectiveness, provider capacity, and the time-dependent operating windows. For E, review all fourteen through last-person extraction and required reception and care. Then review E again from the state produced by N, including provider return or reconfiguration, changed crew functions, deteriorated spaces, and changed access. A favorable U endpoint with failed residual coverage rejects that N variant as a supported presence-preserving plan; it does not automatically reject separately authorized rescue of U. A viable residual crew with late definitive care also fails N's combined purpose. If both schedules pass the physical review, separate authorization, access, and distribution-of-risk judgments still determine whether either should be attempted.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Preserve the political and implementation gates alongside the physical test
reasoning_steps.argument: The revised S-plus proposal in bafe20fc-ca46-4eaf-8d1f-f2a5d717c3df expressly requests protection for N and E through extraction and outbound transit; that is a specification improvement, not accepted access. Bargaining willingness still requires local implementation; authoritative refusal defeats reliance on that package but does not exclude every narrower arrangement; political assent with obstruction defeats reliance on the affected movement until corrected in practice. Medical labeling cannot supply national authorization or settle treaty and use-of-force questions. Equally, uncertain firing order does not logically prevent requesting care or clarifying orders. The supplied ledger's access, authority, legal, attribution, and fallback duties therefore remain unresolved, even if a physical schedule were subsequently supported.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. State the supported conclusion and retained mission limits
reasoning_steps.argument: The current result is an integrated assessment specification and a demonstrated reason independent favorable checks do not suffice. It establishes no actual patient clearance, safe waiting allowance, habitable route, residual roster, or transport window. Confidence is high that those inputs cannot be recovered from the supplied brief; confidence in actual N or E executability remains indeterminate. The earlier conditional survival-first recommendation remains a policy proposal, not an adopted national preference. If safe occupancy is impossible and timely authorized rescue is supported, that proposal favors rescue; without an implemented successor, this may sacrifice physical presence and reward coercion rather than achieve the full mission. Continuing-occupancy repair and evacuation-repair-return remain unimplemented regimes with recurrence, enforcement, and domestic-acceptance obligations. No current finding establishes either durable success or the actual seizure-or-war countermodel.

assumptions: For the integrated physical certificate only, qualified assessments provide valid conservative bounds and constraints for the specified candidate's clinical endpoints, occupied spaces and movement routes, essential crew functions, provider capacities, and operating windows.

For that certificate only, the assessments remain valid over the claimed interval and cover the stated conditions and contingencies, including any proposed wait or N-to-E switch; conditions outside that envelope are not certified.

For that certificate only, a single common schedule satisfies task precedence, durations, movement requirements, resource limits, essential function coverage, operating windows, and every mandatory endpoint bound.
A physical feasibility certificate is limited to its assessed envelope and is not a premise of political cooperation, lawful authorization, guaranteed execution, or assured escalation control.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Define the three candidates and the state they must preserve
reasoning_steps.argument: N selects a departing set Q containing U and every original-crew escort who leaves, with 1 ≤ |Q| < 14, delivers specified effective support, and sustains the remaining personnel through an explicit review horizon h. E removes all fourteen and completes safe reception and indicated care. E after N removes everyone still aboard while also completing the outstanding care obligations for those already departed. At time t, record state x(t): personnel locations and capabilities, patient support needs, safe spaces and routes, available providers and equipment, consumable stocks, ongoing tasks, weather constraints, and assessment validity. Thus E after N is E from x(t), not a fresh copy of E from x(0). If all fourteen must depart for effective care or functional safety, that variant is E rather than N.

reasoning_steps.argument: For each specified provider and mode, define a finite collection of mandatory and contingent tasks, their precedence relations, duration bounds, release conditions, capacity demands, stock consumption, and effects on x(t). Define an uncertainty set Ω describing the conditions for which a certificate is claimed. For the conditional result, qualified assessments must conservatively cover those conditions, including deterioration during waiting and execution. No existence of a feasible schedule is assumed. Provider-specific parameters remain symbolic; no transport mode, replacement crew, operating limit, or assessment outcome is supplied by this model. If the model omits a necessary task or hazard, its certificate does not cover that omission.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Task precedence and patient-care endpoints
reasoning_steps.argument: For task j, let s_j and f_j be its start and finish, with duration determined within the assessed envelope. A precedence edge i → j requires s_j ≥ f_i. A typical transfer chain includes required preparation and support, movement along an assessed route, embarkation, transit, clinical handover, and the clinician-defined intervention endpoint. Receiving-service preparation can occur in parallel, but care cannot be credited before the necessary patient arrival and clinical prerequisites. For every person, define mandatory endpoints for leaving unsafe spaces, supported transfer, reception, and indicated treatment or continuing support. For U, the operative endpoint must be clinician-defined: facility arrival is not surgery. Under N, remaining personnel additionally need effective support and safe occupancy through h. Treatment deadlines may concern initiation or completion; the model must use the endpoint actually specified by clinicians.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Shared resources and inventories
reasoning_steps.argument: For each renewable resource r, require that the total demand of simultaneously active tasks not exceed its available capacity K_r(t, x, ω). Candidate resources include transport capacity, transfer equipment, a usable transfer location, medical attendants, clinical-service capacity, communications capability, and essential crew functions; their actual availability is unknown. A provider transporting U remains committed until its assessed release or return, even after U reaches care. Represent that commitment by an occupation interval or explicit travel and recovery tasks, but do not count it twice. Consumables require stock accounting, not renewable-capacity accounting: delivered usable stock plus initial stock must cover consumption at every time. Support delivered too late, unusable in the occupied space, or consumed by another task cannot also sustain the residual crew.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Residual-crew coverage is a time-dependent assignment constraint
reasoning_steps.argument: Let y_if(t) indicate assignment of person i to essential function f, and let v_if(t, x, ω) indicate qualified, physically accessible, clinically compatible availability. Require y_if ≤ v_if and sufficient coverage for every required function throughout its assessed interval. Impose incompatibility constraints so the same person is not simultaneously credited with mutually exclusive tasks. Required intervals and coverage levels must come from responsible specialists and command, not an invented headcount. A departing escort becomes unavailable aboard; a patient cannot be counted as fit without assessment. Fatigue, movement time, loss of access to a station, and reassignment delays also constrain coverage. N passes only if these assignments work through h and through every transition for which fallback preservation is claimed.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Space, route, and operation-specific weather constraints
reasoning_steps.argument: Each task needs an assessed usable location and, where movement is required, a connected usable route. Every person must occupy an assessed permissible space while aboard, including during waiting. For each operation j, define its permitted weather windows W_j(ω), potentially a union of disjoint intervals. Its actual execution interval must lie within an applicable window, with any stricter continuity requirement explicitly represented. Approach, patient transfer, departure, transit, and reception can have different limits. A route or transfer point may be lost before the wreck sinks; a transfer window may close before the forecast storm arrives. Accordingly, neither six hours nor eighteen hours supplies a model deadline or operating window. Waiting itself must remain physically supportable.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Last-person extraction and shutdown of essential functions
reasoning_steps.argument: For E, let ℓ_i be completion of person i's safe transfer off the wreck and let ℓ_last = max_i ℓ_i. All transfers, including the last, must fit their route, location, weather, and support constraints. The last group must have sufficient capacity and a valid transfer method; no task may silently require an original crew member to remain aboard after that person's own final departure. Essential function coverage persists until a specialist-assessed termination or handover condition, not automatically until everyone else leaves. Any final task must be performable without destroying its performer's extraction route. After ℓ_last, transit, reception, and care obligations can remain outstanding; they continue consuming resources. For E after N, already departed personnel remain in the overall accounting until their mandatory endpoints are completed.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Switching is an explicit transition, not a reset
reasoning_steps.argument: At a switch time τ, preserve every completed action and ongoing commitment in x(τ). Add the necessary switch tasks: communicating the changed plan, safe suspension or completion of ongoing work, recovering or reconfiguring resources, relocating personnel, and preparing the remaining transfers. These can overlap only when their resources and precedence permit. If a single aggregate switch delay δ is used, it must bound those tasks on their actual critical path rather than sum parallel work or omit resource recovery. A switch can occur after a partial N attempt, not only after N completes. The combined schedule must include U's continuing transport and care alongside evacuation of the residual crew. Any claimed protection through the switch also needs separate access and authorization checks.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Information-compatible policies rather than hindsight schedules
reasoning_steps.argument: A policy π maps observed history to authorized candidate actions; physical testing does not itself grant that authorization. For any two modeled states whose observed histories are identical through time t, π must choose identical actions through that time. Observation events must be specified, such as receipt of a particular assessment at θ, an observed provider return, or observed obstruction. If an expected report is delayed or inconclusive, include that history rather than allowing the policy to branch on unavailable information. The physical preservation test is existence of one such policy satisfying the constraints in every ω within its claimed envelope. Separate feasible schedules chosen after learning ω do not establish that policy. Actual task completions may reveal information and permit subsequent adaptation, but an unobserved future deterioration cannot justify an earlier branch-specific dispatch.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Integrated test and its limited soundness
reasoning_steps.argument: Test N alone through its declared horizon, E from the initial state, and a combined N-prefix-to-E policy separately. For the combined claim, require compatible continuation at every history and switch covered by the asserted fallback envelope, not merely at the most convenient switch time. Obtain endpoint completion bounds from that common policy and apply the saved timing certificate in 13e0b524-a2b6-42db-8742-27709383fe8b, cycle 1, steps 4–5. Use the distinct exclusion test in 0825c224-cda6-4e4a-bc77-c148884e9593, cycle 2, step 10, only with its required bound directions. Under valid inputs, a satisfying policy supports the stated physical certificate because each mandatory physical condition is met by compatible actions. Missing inputs or failure to find such a policy leaves certification open. Infeasibility of a conservative model need not establish real physical impossibility; actual exclusion requires a valid unavoidable contradiction for the specified candidate. No completeness over all possible rescue methods is claimed.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Conditional single-provider conflict
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider only this hypothetical candidate family. One provider B is initially available at the wreck. A dedicated U movement started at s ≥ 0 reaches U's required treatment endpoint at s+a and makes B unavailable for further wreck extraction until s+ρ. No substitute or combined loading mode exists within this example. At time θ, an assessment first reveals either continued safe occupancy through the review horizon or deterioration requiring the residual crew's last transfer by H. The residual evacuation requires uninterrupted use of B for duration e; independent switch preparation takes δ after θ and can overlap B's absence. Assume exact symbolic relations a ≤ D_U < θ < ρ and θ+δ+e ≤ H < ρ+e. All other constraints are assumed satisfied for this local example. These are hypothetical relations, not scenario observations.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Derive the conflict and identify the information trap
reasoning_steps.argument: Starting U's dedicated movement at zero meets its deadline because a ≤ D_U. Any timely start must satisfy s ≤ D_U−a < θ, so the dispatch decision precedes the assessment. In the deterioration branch, the residual group's earliest last transfer after dispatch is max(θ+δ, s+ρ)+e. Since s ≥ 0, this is at least ρ+e > H. Thus timely U rescue using this dedicated movement destroys the claimed subsequent evacuation route in that branch. By contrast, θ+δ+e ≤ H shows that the residual evacuation would fit if B were available at θ: the particular obstruction is its continuing commitment to U's movement. A policy cannot dispatch B before θ in the favorable branch but retain it before θ in the adverse branch when those histories are indistinguishable. This refutes that candidate's assured N-to-E fallback, not the value of rescuing U and not every possible assistance policy.

reasoning_steps.title: 14. Bounds that would resolve physical compatibility
reasoning_steps.argument: For a real version of this candidate, certification needs a completion upper bound a+ for U against its deadline lower bound L_U, an absolute upper bound r+ on B's renewed availability, a switch-preparation upper bound δ+, and a compatible residual-extraction upper bound e+. A sufficient last-transfer check is max(θ+δ+, r+)+e+ plus the selected reserve no later than a defensible safe-window/deadline lower bound H−, together with all intermediate windows, coverage, and downstream care checks. Conversely, with unavoidable earliest readiness r−, switch lower bound δ−, extraction lower bound e−, and latest possible transfer deadline H+, max(θ+δ−, r−)+e− > H+ excludes this continuation under those conditions. Here θ must be the actual or properly bounded observation time. A substitute provider's supported readiness and capacity, a valid combined-loading mode, earlier reliable warning, or a different clinically acceptable U route can remove the contradiction, but each changes the candidate and needs its own check. Unknown bounds leave the choice uncertified.

reasoning_steps.title: 15. Direct E and the distribution-of-risk judgment
reasoning_steps.argument: Let direct E have last-transfer completion e0 and U's required-care completion a_E, measured from now. If supported bounds place e0 within every extraction constraint and a_E within U's clinical deadline, and all other endpoints and gates pass, direct E offers a way around this particular resource conflict, though it does not preserve the occupied position. If direct E saves the extraction opportunity but a defensible earliest a_E exceeds U's latest clinical deadline, direct E also fails a mandatory endpoint; it must not be called successful full rescue. Choosing it over dedicated U rescue would then allocate harm differently. The responsible Philippine authorities must explicitly judge exposure of U versus the remaining personnel, the admissibility of an N attempt without an assured fallback, and whether possible physical exclusion is accepted for rescue. Washington and any other provider separately authorize their contributions and exposure. The judgment must identify affected people, unmet endpoints, uncertainty, chosen limits, and delegated emergency decisions if communication fails. A generic survival-first slogan does not resolve that distribution, and no unsupported casualty probabilities or weighted score are supplied here.

reasoning_steps.title: 16. Access, authority, and durable outcomes remain separate
reasoning_steps.argument: Report results as separate fields: physical certificate, implemented access for each movement, legal assessment, Philippine authorization, each provider's national authorization, accepted risk judgment, and durable-mission assessment. S-plus requests N and E protection through last-person extraction and outbound transit; the older N-only specification is stale as a description of the revised request, but its actual-access objection remains unresolved. Bargaining willingness requires acceptance and local implementation; refusal of S-plus does not exclude every narrower arrangement; assent contradicted by obstruction cannot support reliance on that movement. A physical certificate establishes none of these behavioral or legal gates. Continued occupancy additionally needs sustainable repair and repeatable access; evacuation-and-return additionally needs actual protected return and implementation. Evacuation without an implemented successor can preserve lives while sacrificing presence. Reserved claims do not fill that physical gap. Firing order remains unresolved for accountability and legal application, without preventing urgent care requests.

reasoning_steps.title: 17. Provisional decision consequence and ledger disposition
reasoning_steps.argument: The next discriminating analytical test is to evaluate a specified N prefix, direct E, and E after that prefix against the same symbolic task and observation record, expressly identifying the first irreversible resource commitment and the latest supported switch. An affirmative physical result supports consideration, not automatic selection. A proved candidate-specific conflict requires a changed method or an explicit loss-limitation judgment, not continued description of E as assured. The supplied batch's overlapping duties concerning clinical and structural bounds, providers, residual coverage, switching, and last-person extraction are sharpened but remain empirically unresolved. Access, authority, legal sources, attribution, political standards, recurrence, enforceability, domestic acceptance, and historical completeness likewise remain open. In particular, ledger entries e0f2b55cd9d6c187926c0771d2dd71a65c1de224ae0c8ae61aa204b496ef2944 and fd246f7c04254c301e5b947ca8b970b3d0c82b7c189b86207a5d688b9baf92da receive an explicit test, not a positive availability finding. Confidence is high in the conditional resource conflict and information-compatibility distinction, but actual N/E feasibility is indeterminate. Neither durable full success nor the actual seizure-or-war branch is established.
